snapshot.stmt: For triangular treatment-noise laws with \(|\kappa_k(\eta_n)|\ge\delta_n\downarrow0\), determine the sharp minimax MSE phase diagram in \((n,\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n},\delta_n)\) under the same supplied code sequences. defs.def:local-gaussian-handle: Starting from a growing rational library of complex circles, estimate on independent folds each circle's winding number, boundary modulus, and contour-moment variance; use these observable strength diagnostics to construct \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ad}}\) by weak-identification-robust switching among DML, finite-order ACE, and contour moments, and derive the critical scaling when \(|\kappa_k(\eta_n)|\ge\delta_n\downarrow0\).

snapshot.stmt: For \(n\ge2\), suppose \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\) and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\). There are \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), such that \(c/n\le\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\le\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]\le C/n\), uniformly over every deterministic nested \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\). defs.def:contour-bank-handle: Take the locally uniform closure of the centered sub-Gaussian MGFs satisfying \(|\kappa_k|\ge\delta\); for each member choose a rational radius in \((R_0,R_1)\) avoiding its zeros, use Rouche stability to form a compact-open neighborhood preserving positive zero count and boundary separation, extract a finite subcover, retain its radii \(\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_J\), and define \(a_{\star}\) as one half of the smallest retained boundary modulus.

defs.def:jms-eligibility: Compute \(a_{1,n},b_{1,n},a_2,b_{2,n}\) exactly as in condition (21) and set \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) to the condition \(r\le\min\{b_{1,n}/a_{1,n}-a_{1,n}^{-1}\log(b_{1,n}/a_{1,n}),b_{2,n}/[a_2\log(a_2b_{2,n})]\}\) on indices for which these expressions are defined.

defs.def:gaussian-class: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}=\{P:E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0,\ |\theta_0|\le C_{\theta},\ |Y|\le C_q,\ \eta\perp X,\ \eta\sim N(0,\sigma^2),\ \|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g,\ \|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n},\ \|\bar q_n-q_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}\}\) within the published PLM, with \(g_0,q_0,\eta,\xi\) given by their displayed residual definitions. snapshot.stmt: For \(s\ge r+1\), every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) satisfies the \(L^r(P_X)\) code controls needed to test membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\), because \(\|f\|_{L^r(P_X)}\le\|f\|_{L^s(P_X)}\). snapshot.stmt:
The following two conclusions are valid, but they do not determine the full-class minimax phase diagram.

First, for each \(n\), let \(\mathcal C_n(\delta_n)\) be the class obtained from \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in \(\text{def:jms-ace-class}\) by replacing the fixed restriction \(\lvert\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)\rvert\ge\delta\) by \(\lvert\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)\rvert\ge\delta_n\), without changing any other restriction.  Define
\[
 \widetilde b_{2,n}
 =200\min\{1,C_{\theta}\}\delta_n
 \max\!\left\{
   \varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n},
   (\gamma n)^{-1/2}(\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta})
 \right\}^{-1}.
\]
Suppose \(\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n}>0\), all logarithms and denominators in the following display are defined, and the exact local eligibility condition
\[
 r\le
 \min\!\left\{
   \frac{b_{1,n}}{a_{1,n}}
   -\frac{1}{a_{1,n}}\log\!\left(\frac{b_{1,n}}{a_{1,n}}\right),
   \frac{\widetilde b_{2,n}}{a_2\log(a_2\widetilde b_{2,n})}
 \right\}
\]
holds.  Then the order-\(r\) ACE estimator obeys the local oracle benchmark
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{P\in\mathcal C_n(\delta_n)}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}
 \!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)\\
 &\quad\le
 C_{\gamma}r!6^r\delta_n^{-1}
 \Bigl[
   \varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
   +C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}\\
 &\hspace{42mm}
   +4(C_g+\psi_{\eta})^r
    \{r^2(C_g+\psi_{\eta})+\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta}\}
    (\gamma n)^{-1/2}
 \Bigr].
\end{aligned}
\]
Denote the right-hand side by \(U_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{loc}}\).  If \(U_{\mathrm{DML},n}\) denotes a separately valid ordinary-DML upper bound under its own hypotheses, then \(\min\{U_{\mathrm{DML},n},U_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{loc}}\}\) is only an oracle upper envelope; this comparison neither asserts a minimax rate nor constructs a data-driven selector.

Second, specialize to \(k=4\), hence \(r=3\).  For \(0<a\le1\), let
\[
 \eta_a=\sqrt{1-a^2}\,G_{\circ}+aS,
\]
where \(G_{\circ}\sim N(0,1)\), \(S\) is symmetric Rademacher, and \(G_{\circ}\perp S\).  Its moment generating function, fourth cumulant, and first positive characteristic zero are
\[
 M_a(z)=\exp\!\left(\frac{1-a^2}{2}z^2\right)\cosh(az),
 \qquad
 \kappa_4(\eta_a)=-2a^4,
 \qquad
 t_a=\frac{\pi}{2a}.
\]
For every real \(d\),
\[
 E\!\left[\sin\{t_a(\eta_a+d)\}\right]=0.
\]
Consider any law satisfying \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\), \(\eta=\eta_a\perp X\), \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\) almost surely, \(\lvert\theta_0(P)\rvert\le C_{\theta}\), \(\lVert g_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_g\), \(\lVert q_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_q\), \(\lVert\xi\rVert_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}\) almost surely, and \(\lVert\bar g_n-g_0\rVert_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\).  Put
\[
 A_a=a\exp\!\left\{-\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{8a^2}\right\}.
\]
If \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le1/2\), then
\[
 E_P\!\left[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)\right]
 =A_aE_P[\cos(t_aD_n)]
 \ge\frac{A_a}{2}.
\]
Writing \(\mathbb P_n\) for the empirical average, define the computable clipped ratio
\[
 \widehat\theta_{a,n}
 =
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle
 \Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}
 \frac{\mathbb P_n[Y\sin(t_aZ_n)]}
      {\mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]},
 &\displaystyle
 \mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]\ge A_a/4,\\[3mm]
 0,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\]
There is a finite constant \(C\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), such that
\[
 \sup_P E_P\!\left[(\widehat\theta_{a,n}-\theta_0(P))^2\right]
 \le
 C\min\!\left\{
  1,\frac{1}{n}a^{-2}
  \exp\!\left(\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{4a^2}\right)
 \right\},
\]
where the supremum is over the just-displayed path laws.  Equivalently, with \(\Delta_a=2a^4=\lvert\kappa_4(\eta_a)\rvert\), the condition \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le1/2\) is
\[
 \varepsilon_{1,n}\le\frac{\Delta_a^{1/4}}{2^{1/4}\pi},
\]
and the preceding risk is at most
\[
 C\min\!\left\{
  1,\frac{1}{n}\Delta_a^{-1/2}
  \exp\!\left(\frac{\pi^2\sqrt2}{4}\Delta_a^{-1/2}\right)
 \right\}.
\]
This last display is a construction-specific upper bound with \(\varepsilon_{1,n}=O(\Delta_a^{1/4})\); it is not asserted to be sharp for the class specified only by a fourth-cumulant lower bound.

snapshot.stmt: For triangular treatment-noise laws with \(|\kappa_k(\eta_n)|\ge\delta_n\downarrow0\), determine the sharp minimax MSE phase diagram in \((n,\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n},\delta_n)\) under the same supplied code sequences. Can the handle in \(\text{def:local-gaussian-handle}\) produce \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ad}}\) with uniform valid inference across DML, finite-order ACE, and global-contour regimes, together with matching lower bounds?

defs.def:local-gaussian-handle: Starting from a growing rational library of complex circles, estimate on independent folds each circle's winding number, boundary modulus, and contour-moment variance; use these observable strength diagnostics to construct \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ad}}\) by weak-identification-robust switching among DML, finite-order ACE, and contour moments, and derive the critical scaling when \(|\kappa_k(\eta_n)|\ge\delta_n\downarrow0\).

snapshot.stmt:
The following two conclusions are valid, but they do not determine the full-class minimax phase diagram.

First, for each \(n\), let \(\mathcal C_n(\delta_n)\) be the class obtained from \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in \(\text{def:jms-ace-class}\) by replacing the fixed restriction \(\lvert\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)\rvert\ge\delta\) by \(\lvert\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)\rvert\ge\delta_n\), without changing any other restriction.  Define
\[
 \widetilde b_{2,n}
 =200\min\{1,C_{\theta}\}\delta_n
 \max\!\left\{
   \varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n},
   (\gamma n)^{-1/2}(\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta})
 \right\}^{-1}.
\]
Suppose \(\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n}>0\), all logarithms and denominators in the following display are defined, and the exact local eligibility condition
\[
 r\le
 \min\!\left\{
   \frac{b_{1,n}}{a_{1,n}}
   -\frac{1}{a_{1,n}}\log\!\left(\frac{b_{1,n}}{a_{1,n}}\right),
   \frac{\widetilde b_{2,n}}{a_2\log(a_2\widetilde b_{2,n})}
 \right\}
\]
holds.  Then the order-\(r\) ACE estimator obeys the local oracle benchmark
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{P\in\mathcal C_n(\delta_n)}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}
 \!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)\\
 &\quad\le
 C_{\gamma}r!16^r\delta_n^{-1}
 \Bigl[
   \varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
   +C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}\\
 &\hspace{42mm}
   +64(C_g+\psi_{\eta})^r
    \{r^2(C_g+\psi_{\eta})+\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta}\}
    (\gamma n)^{-1/2}
 \Bigr].
\end{aligned}
\]
Denote the right-hand side by \(U_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{loc}}\).  If \(U_{\mathrm{DML},n}\) denotes a separately valid ordinary-DML upper bound under its own hypotheses, then \(\min\{U_{\mathrm{DML},n},U_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{loc}}\}\) is only an oracle upper envelope; this comparison neither asserts a minimax rate nor constructs a data-driven selector.

Second, specialize to \(k=4\), hence \(r=3\).  For \(0<a\le1\), let
\[
 \eta_a=\sqrt{1-a^2}\,G_{\circ}+aS,
\]
where \(G_{\circ}\sim N(0,1)\), \(S\) is symmetric Rademacher, and \(G_{\circ}\perp S\).  Its moment generating function, fourth cumulant, and first positive characteristic zero are
\[
 M_a(z)=\exp\!\left(\frac{1-a^2}{2}z^2\right)\cosh(az),
 \qquad
 \kappa_4(\eta_a)=-2a^4,
 \qquad
 t_a=\frac{\pi}{2a}.
\]
For every real \(d\),
\[
 E\!\left[\sin\{t_a(\eta_a+d)\}\right]=0.
\]
Consider any law satisfying \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\), \(\eta=\eta_a\perp X\), \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\) almost surely, \(\lvert\theta_0(P)\rvert\le C_{\theta}\), \(\lVert g_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_g\), \(\lVert q_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_q\), \(\lVert\xi\rVert_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}\) almost surely, and \(\lVert\bar g_n-g_0\rVert_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\).  Put
\[
 A_a=a\exp\!\left\{-\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{8a^2}\right\}.
\]
If \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le1/2\), then
\[
 E_P\!\left[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)\right]
 =A_aE_P[\cos(t_aD_n)]
 \ge\frac{A_a}{2}.
\]
Writing \(\mathbb P_n\) for the empirical average, define the computable clipped ratio
\[
 \widehat\theta_{a,n}
 =
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle
 \Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}
 \frac{\mathbb P_n[Y\sin(t_aZ_n)]}
      {\mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]},
 &\displaystyle
 \mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]\ge A_a/4,\\[3mm]
 0,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\]
There is a finite constant \(C\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), such that
\[
 \sup_P E_P\!\left[(\widehat\theta_{a,n}-\theta_0(P))^2\right]
 \le
 C\min\!\left\{
  1,\frac{1}{n}a^{-2}
  \exp\!\left(\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{4a^2}\right)
 \right\},
\]
where the supremum is over the just-displayed path laws.  Equivalently, with \(\Delta_a=2a^4=\lvert\kappa_4(\eta_a)\rvert\), the condition \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le1/2\) is
\[
 \varepsilon_{1,n}\le\frac{\Delta_a^{1/4}}{2^{1/4}\pi},
\]
and the preceding risk is at most
\[
 C\min\!\left\{
  1,\frac{1}{n}\Delta_a^{-1/2}
  \exp\!\left(\frac{\pi^2\sqrt2}{4}\Delta_a^{-1/2}\right)
 \right\}.
\]
This last display is a construction-specific upper bound with \(\varepsilon_{1,n}=O(\Delta_a^{1/4})\); it is not asserted to be sharp for the class specified only by a fourth-cumulant lower bound.

snapshot.stmt: For \(n\ge2\), suppose \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\) and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\). There are \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), such that \(c/n\le\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\le\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]\le C/n\), uniformly over every deterministic nested \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\). The estimator uses \(\bar g_n\), does not use \(\bar q_n\), and does not know the law of \(\eta\). Its MSE bound implies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)\le\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}\). Because \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\), every index satisfying \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) obeys \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)|)\le B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}\), including \(\varepsilon_{2,n}=0\) by monotone boundary extension. Thus throughout \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) the spectral guarantee removes the two nuisance terms appearing in Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis bound (22); whenever \(\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}+C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}\gg n^{-1/2}\), it is strictly smaller in order than \(B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}\).

defs.def:adaptive-contour-estimator: Compute \(\widehat F_{a,n}\) and \(\widehat G_{a,n}\) on \(I_a\). Declare \(j\) pilot-admissible when \(\inf_{z\in C_j}|\widehat F_{0,n}(z)|\ge a_{\star}/2\) and \(\widehat N_{0j,n}\ge1\). Let \(\widehat j_n\) be the smallest maximizer of the pilot boundary modulus over admissible indices. Return zero if the set is empty or if \(\inf_{z\in C_{\widehat j_n}}|\widehat F_{1,n}(z)|<a_{\star}/4\); otherwise return \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}=\Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}\operatorname{Re}[\{\widehat N_{0\widehat j_n,n}2\pi i\}^{-1}\oint_{C_{\widehat j_n}}\widehat G_{1,n}(z)/\widehat F_{1,n}(z)\,dz]\). Ties and failure events use the displayed deterministic rules, making the finite-bank selector measurable once the contour integrals are represented by fixed parametrizations.

snapshot.stmt:
The following two conclusions are valid, but they do not determine the full-class minimax phase diagram.

First, for each \(n\), let \(\mathcal C_n(\delta_n)\) be the class obtained from \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in \(\text{def:jms-ace-class}\) by replacing the fixed restriction \(\lvert\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)\rvert\ge\delta\) by \(\lvert\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)\rvert\ge\delta_n\), without changing any other restriction.  Define
\[
 \widetilde b_{2,n}
 =200\min\{1,C_{\theta}\}\delta_n
 \max\!\left\{
   \varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n},
   (\gamma n)^{-1/2}(\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta})
 \right\}^{-1}.
\]
Suppose \(\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n}>0\), all logarithms and denominators in the following display are defined, and the exact local eligibility condition
\[
 r\le
 \min\!\left\{
   \frac{b_{1,n}}{a_{1,n}}
   -\frac{1}{a_{1,n}}\log\!\left(\frac{b_{1,n}}{a_{1,n}}\right),
   \frac{\widetilde b_{2,n}}{a_2\log(a_2\widetilde b_{2,n})}
 \right\}
\]
holds.  Then the order-\(r\) ACE estimator obeys the local oracle benchmark
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{P\in\mathcal C_n(\delta_n)}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}
 \!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)\\
 &\quad\le
 C_{\gamma}r!16^r\delta_n^{-1}
 \Bigl[
   \varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
   +C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}\\
 &\hspace{42mm}
   +64(C_g+\psi_{\eta})^r
    \{r^2(C_g+\psi_{\eta})+\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta}\}
    (\gamma n)^{-1/2}
 \Bigr].
\end{aligned}
\]
Denote the right-hand side by \(U_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{loc}}\).  If \(U_{\mathrm{DML},n}\) denotes a separately valid ordinary-DML upper bound under its own hypotheses, then \(\min\{U_{\mathrm{DML},n},U_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{loc}}\}\) is only an oracle upper envelope; this comparison neither asserts a minimax rate nor constructs a data-driven selector.

Second, specialize to \(k=4\), hence \(r=3\).  For \(0<a\le1\), let
\[
 \eta_a=\sqrt{1-a^2}\,G_{\circ}+aS,
\]
where \(G_{\circ}\sim N(0,1)\), \(S\) is symmetric Rademacher, and \(G_{\circ}\perp S\).  Its moment generating function, fourth cumulant, and first positive characteristic zero are
\[
 M_a(z)=\exp\!\left(\frac{1-a^2}{2}z^2\right)\cosh(az),
 \qquad
 \kappa_4(\eta_a)=-2a^4,
 \qquad
 t_a=\frac{\pi}{2a}.
\]
For every real \(d\),
\[
 E\!\left[\sin\{t_a(\eta_a+d)\}\right]=0.
\]
Consider any law satisfying \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\), \(\eta=\eta_a\perp X\), \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\) almost surely, \(\lvert\theta_0(P)\rvert\le C_{\theta}\), \(\lVert g_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_g\), \(\lVert q_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_q\), \(\lVert\xi\rVert_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}\) almost surely, and \(\lVert\bar g_n-g_0\rVert_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\).  Put
\[
 A_a=a\exp\!\left\{-\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{8a^2}\right\}.
\]
If \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le1/2\), then
\[
 E_P\!\left[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)\right]
 =A_aE_P[\cos(t_aD_n)]
 \ge\frac{A_a}{2}.
\]
Writing \(\mathbb P_n\) for the empirical average, define the computable clipped ratio
\[
 \widehat\theta_{a,n}
 =
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle
 \Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}
 \frac{\mathbb P_n[Y\sin(t_aZ_n)]}
      {\mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]},
 &\displaystyle
 \mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]\ge A_a/4,\\[3mm]
 0,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\]
There is a finite constant \(C\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), such that
\[
 \sup_P E_P\!\left[(\widehat\theta_{a,n}-\theta_0(P))^2\right]
 \le
 C\min\!\left\{
  1,\frac{1}{n}a^{-2}
  \exp\!\left(\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{4a^2}\right)
 \right\},
\]
where the supremum is over the just-displayed path laws.  Equivalently, with \(\Delta_a=2a^4=\lvert\kappa_4(\eta_a)\rvert\), the condition \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le1/2\) is
\[
 \varepsilon_{1,n}\le\frac{\Delta_a^{1/4}}{2^{1/4}\pi},
\]
and the preceding risk is at most
\[
 C\min\!\left\{
  1,\frac{1}{n}\Delta_a^{-1/2}
  \exp\!\left(\frac{\pi^2\sqrt2}{4}\Delta_a^{-1/2}\right)
 \right\}.
\]
This last display is a construction-specific upper bound with \(\varepsilon_{1,n}=O(\Delta_a^{1/4})\); it is not asserted to be sharp for the class specified only by a fourth-cumulant lower bound.

\begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{P\in\mathcal C_n(\delta_n)}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}
 \!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)\\
 &\quad\le
 C_{\gamma}r!16^r\delta_n^{-1}
 \Bigl[
   \varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
   +C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}\\
 &\hspace{42mm}
   +64(C_g+\psi_{\eta})^r
    \{r^2(C_g+\psi_{\eta})+\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta}\}
    (\gamma n)^{-1/2}
 \Bigr].
\end{aligned}
\]
Denote the right-hand side by \(U_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{loc}}\).  If \(U_{\mathrm{DML},n}\) denotes a separately valid ordinary-DML upper bound under its own hypotheses, then \(\min\{U_{\mathrm{DML},n},U_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{loc}}\}\) is only an oracle upper envelope; this comparison neither asserts a minimax rate nor constructs a data-driven selector.

Second, specialize to \(k=4\), hence \(r=3\).  For \(0<a\le1\), let
\[
 \eta_a=\sqrt{1-a^2}\,G_{\circ}+aS,
\]
where \(G_{\circ}\sim N(0,1)\), \(S\) is symmetric Rademacher, and \(G_{\circ}\perp S\).  Its moment generating function, fourth cumulant, and first positive characteristic zero are
\[
 M_a(z)=\exp\!\left(\frac{1-a^2}{2}z^2\right)\cosh(az),
 \qquad
 \kappa_4(\eta_a)=-2a^4,
 \qquad
 t_a=\frac{\pi}{2a}.
\]
For every real \(d\),
\[
 E\!\left[\sin\{t_a(\eta_a+d)\}\right]=0.
\]
Consider any law satisfying \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\), \(\eta=\eta_a\perp X\), \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\) almost surely, \(\lvert\theta_0(P)\rvert\le C_{\theta}\), \(\lVert g_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_g\), \(\lVert q_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_q\), \(\lVert\xi\rVert_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}\) almost surely, and \(\lVert\bar g_n-g_0\rVert_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\).  Put
\[
 A_a=a\exp\!\left\{-\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{8a^2}\right\}.
\]
If \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le1/2\), then
\[
 E_P\!\left[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)\right]
 =A_aE_P[\cos(t_aD_n)]
 \ge\frac{A_a}{2}.
\]
Writing \(\mathbb P_n\) for the empirical average, define the computable clipped ratio
\[
 \widehat\theta_{a,n}
 =
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle
 \Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}
 \frac{\mathbb P_n[Y\sin(t_aZ_n)]}
      {\mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]},
 &\displaystyle
 \mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]\ge A_a/4,\\[3mm]
 0,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\]
There is a finite constant \(C\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), such that
\[
 \sup_P E_P\!\left[(\widehat\theta_{a,n}-\theta_0(P))^2\right]
 \le
 C\min\!\left\{
  1,\frac{1}{n}a^{-2}
  \exp\!\left(\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{4a^2}\right)
 \right\},
\]
where the supremum is over the just-displayed path laws.  Equivalently, with \(\Delta_a=2a^4=\lvert\kappa_4(\eta_a)\rvert\), the condition \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le1/2\) is
\[
 \varepsilon_{1,n}\le\frac{\Delta_a^{1/4}}{2^{1/4}\pi},
\]
and the preceding risk is at most
\[
 C\min\!\left\{
  1,\frac{1}{n}\Delta_a^{-1/2}
  \exp\!\left(\frac{\pi^2\sqrt2}{4}\Delta_a^{-1/2}\right)
 \right\}.
\]
This last display is a construction-specific upper bound with \(\varepsilon_{1,n}=O(\Delta_a^{1/4})\); it is not asserted to be sharp for the class specified only by a fourth-cumulant lower bound.

snapshot.stmt: The construction in \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) yields finite \(J\), radii \(R_0<\rho_j<R_1\), and \(a_{\star}>0\) such that every treatment-noise transform represented in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) has some \(j\) with \(N_{C_j}(M)\ge1\) and \(\inf_{z\in C_j}|M(z)|\ge a_{\star}\). snapshot.stmt:
For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), the class's \(L^1(P_X)\) treatment-code restriction and clipping imply \(|D_n|\le2C_g\) almost surely and \(E_P|D_n|\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\). Hence
\[
 \sup_{|z|\le R_1}|H_n(z)-1|
 \le R_1e^{2C_gR_1}\varepsilon_{1,n}.

If \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\), then \(|H_n(z)|\ge3/4\) throughout \(\{|z|\le R_1\}\), and \(F_n=M H_n\) and \(M\) have the same zeros there with multiplicity.

snapshot.stmt:

 \le\frac Cn.
\]

\[

 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)

snapshot.stmt:
For every \(n\) such that \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le 1/\pi\), let \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\). Suppose that \(\eta\sim\tfrac12N(-1,1)+\tfrac12N(1,1)\), \(\eta\perp X\), \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\) almost surely, \(|\theta_0(P)|\le C_{\theta}\), \(\|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g\), \(\|q_0\|_{\infty}\le C_q\), \(\|\xi\|_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}\) almost surely, and \(\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\). Then \(\kappa_4(\eta)=-2\), \(M(i\pi/2)=0\), and
\[
E_P\!\left[Z_n\sin\!\left(\frac{\pi Z_n}{2}\right)\right]
=e^{-\pi^2/8}E_P\!\left[\cos\!\left(\frac{\pi D_n}{2}\right)\right]
\ge \frac12e^{-\pi^2/8}.
\]
There is a finite constant \(C\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), such that, uniformly over all laws \(P\) satisfying the preceding conditions,
\[
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\theta_{\sin,n}-\theta_0(P))^2\right]\le \frac{C}{n}.
\]
No condition on the supplied outcome code or on \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\) is required.

defs.def:sine-estimator: \(\widehat\theta_{\sin,n}=\Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}\{\mathbb P_n[Y\sin(\pi Z_n/2)]/\mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(\pi Z_n/2)]\}\), with fallback zero when the empirical denominator is below one half of its population lower bound.

 =\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}

\]

snapshot.stmt:
The following two conclusions are valid, but they do not determine the full-class minimax phase diagram.

First, for each \(n\), let \(\mathcal C_n(\delta_n)\) be the class obtained from \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in \(\text{def:jms-ace-class}\) by replacing the fixed restriction \(\lvert\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)\rvert\ge\delta\) by \(\lvert\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)\rvert\ge\delta_n\), without changing any other restriction.  Define
\[
 \widetilde b_{2,n}
 =200\min\{1,C_{\theta}\}\delta_n
 \max\!\left\{
   \varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n},
   (\gamma n)^{-1/2}(\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta})
 \right\}^{-1}.
\]
Suppose \(\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n}>0\), all logarithms and denominators in the following display are defined, and the exact local eligibility condition
\[
 r\le
 \min\!\left\{
   \frac{b_{1,n}}{a_{1,n}}
   -\frac{1}{a_{1,n}}\log\!\left(\frac{b_{1,n}}{a_{1,n}}\right),
   \frac{\widetilde b_{2,n}}{a_2\log(a_2\widetilde b_{2,n})}
 \right\}
\]
holds.  Then the order-\(r\) ACE estimator obeys the local oracle benchmark
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{P\in\mathcal C_n(\delta_n)}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}
 \!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)\\
 &\quad\le
 C_{\gamma}r!16^r\delta_n^{-1}
 \Bigl[
   \varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
   +C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}\\
 &\hspace{42mm}
   +64(C_g+\psi_{\eta})^r
    \{r^2(C_g+\psi_{\eta})+\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta}\}
    (\gamma n)^{-1/2}
 \Bigr].
\end{aligned}
\]
Denote the right-hand side by \(U_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{loc}}\).  If \(U_{\mathrm{DML},n}\) denotes a separately valid ordinary-DML upper bound under its own hypotheses, then \(\min\{U_{\mathrm{DML},n},U_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{loc}}\}\) is only an oracle upper envelope; this comparison neither asserts a minimax rate nor constructs a data-driven selector.

Second, specialize to \(k=4\), hence \(r=3\).  For \(0<a\le1\), let
\[
 \eta_a=\sqrt{1-a^2}\,G_{\circ}+aS,
\]
where \(G_{\circ}\sim N(0,1)\), \(S\) is symmetric Rademacher, and \(G_{\circ}\perp S\).  Its moment generating function, fourth cumulant, and first positive characteristic zero are
\[
 M_a(z)=\exp\!\left(\frac{1-a^2}{2}z^2\right)\cosh(az),
 \qquad
 \kappa_4(\eta_a)=-2a^4,
 \qquad
 t_a=\frac{\pi}{2a}.
\]
For every real \(d\),
\[
 E\!\left[\sin\{t_a(\eta_a+d)\}\right]=0.
\]
Consider any law satisfying \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\), \(\eta=\eta_a\perp X\), \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\) almost surely, \(\lvert\theta_0(P)\rvert\le C_{\theta}\), \(\lVert g_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_g\), \(\lVert q_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_q\), \(\lVert\xi\rVert_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}\) almost surely, and \(\lVert\bar g_n-g_0\rVert_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\).  Put
\[
 A_a=a\exp\!\left\{-\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{8a^2}\right\}.
\]
If \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le1/2\), then
\[
 E_P\!\left[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)\right]
 =A_aE_P[\cos(t_aD_n)]
 \ge\frac{A_a}{2}.
\]
Writing \(\mathbb P_n\) for the empirical average, define the computable clipped ratio
\[
 \widehat\theta_{a,n}
 =
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle
 \Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}
 \frac{\mathbb P_n[Y\sin(t_aZ_n)]}
      {\mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]},
 &\displaystyle
 \mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]\ge A_a/4,\\[3mm]
 0,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\]
There is a finite constant \(C\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), such that
\[
 \sup_P E_P\!\left[(\widehat\theta_{a,n}-\theta_0(P))^2\right]
 \le
 C\min\!\left\{
  1,\frac{1}{n}a^{-2}
  \exp\!\left(\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{4a^2}\right)
 \right\},
\]
where the supremum is over the just-displayed path laws.  Equivalently, with \(\Delta_a=2a^4=\lvert\kappa_4(\eta_a)\rvert\), the condition \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le1/2\) is
\[
 \varepsilon_{1,n}\le\frac{\Delta_a^{1/4}}{2^{1/4}\pi},
\]
and the preceding risk is at most
\[
 C\min\!\left\{
  1,\frac{1}{n}\Delta_a^{-1/2}
  \exp\!\left(\frac{\pi^2\sqrt2}{4}\Delta_a^{-1/2}\right)
 \right\}.
\]
This last display is a construction-specific upper bound with \(\varepsilon_{1,n}=O(\Delta_a^{1/4})\); it is not asserted to be sharp for the class specified only by a fourth-cumulant lower bound.

Can the handle in \(\text{def:local-gaussian-handle}\) produce \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ad}}\) with uniform valid inference across DML, finite-order ACE, and global-contour regimes, together with matching lower bounds?

defs.def:local-gaussian-handle: Starting from a growing rational library of complex circles, estimate on independent folds each circle's winding number, boundary modulus, and contour-moment variance; use these observable strength diagnostics to construct \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ad}}\) by weak-identification-robust switching among DML, finite-order ACE, and contour moments, and derive the critical scaling when \(|\kappa_k(\eta_n)|\ge\delta_n\downarrow0\).

snapshot.stmt:
The following two conclusions are valid, but they do not determine the full-class minimax phase diagram.

First, for each \(n\), let \(\mathcal C_n(\delta_n)\) be the class obtained from \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in \(\text{def:jms-ace-class}\) by replacing the fixed restriction \(\lvert\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)\rvert\ge\delta\) by \(\lvert\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)\rvert\ge\delta_n\), without changing any other restriction.  Define
\[
 \widetilde b_{2,n}
 =200\min\{1,C_{\theta}\}\delta_n
 \max\!\left\{
   \varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n},
   (\gamma n)^{-1/2}(\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta})
 \right\}^{-1}.
\]
Suppose \(\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n}>0\), all logarithms and denominators in the following display are defined, and the exact local eligibility condition
\[
 r\le
 \min\!\left\{
   \frac{b_{1,n}}{a_{1,n}}
   -\frac{1}{a_{1,n}}\log\!\left(\frac{b_{1,n}}{a_{1,n}}\right),
   \frac{\widetilde b_{2,n}}{a_2\log(a_2\widetilde b_{2,n})}
 \right\}
\]
holds.  Then the order-\(r\) ACE estimator obeys the local oracle benchmark
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{P\in\mathcal C_n(\delta_n)}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}
 \!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)\\
 &\quad\le
 C_{\gamma}r!16^r\delta_n^{-1}
 \Bigl[
   \varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
   +C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}\\
 &\hspace{42mm}
   +64(C_g+\psi_{\eta})^r
    \{r^2(C_g+\psi_{\eta})+\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta}\}
    (\gamma n)^{-1/2}
 \Bigr].
\end{aligned}
\]
Denote the right-hand side by \(U_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{loc}}\).  If \(U_{\mathrm{DML},n}\) denotes a separately valid ordinary-DML upper bound under its own hypotheses, then \(\min\{U_{\mathrm{DML},n},U_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{loc}}\}\) is only an oracle upper envelope; this comparison neither asserts a minimax rate nor constructs a data-driven selector.

Second, specialize to \(k=4\), hence \(r=3\).  For \(0<a\le1\), let
\[
 \eta_a=\sqrt{1-a^2}\,G_{\circ}+aS,
\]
where \(G_{\circ}\sim N(0,1)\), \(S\) is symmetric Rademacher, and \(G_{\circ}\perp S\).  Its moment generating function, fourth cumulant, and first positive characteristic zero are
\[
 M_a(z)=\exp\!\left(\frac{1-a^2}{2}z^2\right)\cosh(az),
 \qquad
 \kappa_4(\eta_a)=-2a^4,
 \qquad
 t_a=\frac{\pi}{2a}.
\]
For every real \(d\),
\[
 E\!\left[\sin\{t_a(\eta_a+d)\}\right]=0.
\]
Consider any law satisfying \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\), \(\eta=\eta_a\perp X\), \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\) almost surely, \(\lvert\theta_0(P)\rvert\le C_{\theta}\), \(\lVert g_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_g\), \(\lVert q_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_q\), \(\lVert\xi\rVert_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}\) almost surely, and \(\lVert\bar g_n-g_0\rVert_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\).  Put
\[
 A_a=a\exp\!\left\{-\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{8a^2}\right\}.
\]
If \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le1/2\), then
\[
 E_P\!\left[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)\right]
 =A_aE_P[\cos(t_aD_n)]
 \ge\frac{A_a}{2}.
\]
Writing \(\mathbb P_n\) for the empirical average, define the computable clipped ratio
\[
 \widehat\theta_{a,n}
 =
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle
 \Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}
 \frac{\mathbb P_n[Y\sin(t_aZ_n)]}
      {\mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]},
 &\displaystyle
 \mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]\ge A_a/4,\\[3mm]
 0,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\]
There is a finite constant \(C\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), such that
\[
 \sup_P E_P\!\left[(\widehat\theta_{a,n}-\theta_0(P))^2\right]
 \le
 C\min\!\left\{
  1,\frac{1}{n}a^{-2}
  \exp\!\left(\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{4a^2}\right)
 \right\},
\]
where the supremum is over the just-displayed path laws.  Equivalently, with \(\Delta_a=2a^4=\lvert\kappa_4(\eta_a)\rvert\), the condition \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le1/2\) is
\[
 \varepsilon_{1,n}\le\frac{\Delta_a^{1/4}}{2^{1/4}\pi},
\]
and the preceding risk is at most
\[
 C\min\!\left\{
  1,\frac{1}{n}\Delta_a^{-1/2}
  \exp\!\left(\frac{\pi^2\sqrt2}{4}\Delta_a^{-1/2}\right)
 \right\}.
\]
This last display is a construction-specific upper bound with \(\varepsilon_{1,n}=O(\Delta_a^{1/4})\); it is not asserted to be sharp for the class specified only by a fourth-cumulant lower bound.

snapshot.stmt:
For every \(n\) such that \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le 1/\pi\), let \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\). Suppose that \(\eta\sim\tfrac12N(-1,1)+\tfrac12N(1,1)\), \(\eta\perp X\), \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\) almost surely, \(|\theta_0(P)|\le C_{\theta}\), \(\|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g\), \(\|q_0\|_{\infty}\le C_q\), \(\|\xi\|_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}\) almost surely, and \(\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\). Then \(\kappa_4(\eta)=-2\), \(M(i\pi/2)=0\), and
\[
E_P\!\left[Z_n\sin\!\left(\frac{\pi Z_n}{2}\right)\right]
=e^{-\pi^2/8}E_P\!\left[\cos\!\left(\frac{\pi D_n}{2}\right)\right]
\ge \frac12e^{-\pi^2/8}.
\]
There is a finite constant \(C\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), such that, uniformly over all laws \(P\) satisfying the preceding conditions,
\[
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\theta_{\sin,n}-\theta_0(P))^2\right]\le \frac{C}{n}.
\]
No condition on the supplied outcome code or on \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\) is required.

defs.def:sine-estimator: \(\widehat\theta_{\sin,n}=\Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}\{\mathbb P_n[Y\sin(\pi Z_n/2)]/\mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(\pi Z_n/2)]\}\), with fallback zero when the empirical denominator is below one half of its population lower bound.

snapshot.stmt:
For \(n\ge2\), suppose \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\) and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\). There are \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), such that
\[
 \frac cn\le\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}
 \le\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le\frac Cn.
\]
The estimator uses \(\bar g_n\), uses no supplied outcome code, and does not know the law of \(\eta\). Its MSE bound implies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)
 \le\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}.
\]
No inclusion of the broad class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is asserted; the finite-order ACE comparison is confined to the separately defined subclass \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\).

defs.def:ace-comparison-subclass: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}=\{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}:\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n},\ \|\bar q_n-q_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}\}\). Thus this comparison class restores both supplied-code restrictions while retaining every condition of the broad spectral class.
defs.def:contour-bank-handle: Let \(\mathscr M\) be the locally uniform closure of the centered sub-Gaussian moment generating functions satisfying \(\lvert\kappa_k\rvert\ge\delta\).  A once-for-all contour bank is a tuple consisting of a finite \(J\ge1\), radii \((\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_J)\in(R_0,R_1)^J\), and \(a_{\star}>0\) such that, with \(C_j=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=\rho_j\}\), every \(M\in\mathscr M\) has some \(j\) for which \(N_{C_j}(M)\ge1\) and \(\inf_{z\in C_j}|M(z)|\ge a_{\star}\).  After \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\) proves that such tuples exist, fix one arbitrary tuple and denote it by \((J,\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_J,a_{\star})\).  The choice is deterministic and depends only on the class constants \((k,\delta,\psi_{\eta},R_0,R_1)\); no effective enumeration, computable radii, computable modulus, or algorithm for finding the tuple is asserted.
defs.def:minimax-risks: \(\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}=\inf_{\widetilde\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_n;\bar g_n,\bar q_n)}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}E_P[(\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P))^2]\), \(\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}=\inf_{\widetilde\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_n;\bar g_n,\bar q_n)}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}E_P[(\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P))^2]\), and \(\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}=\inf_{\widetilde\theta}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P)|)\).
defs.def:non-gaussian-class: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}=\{P: \eta\perp X,\ E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0,\ |\theta_0|\le C_{\theta},\ \|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g,\ \|q_0\|_{\infty}\le C_q,\ \|\eta\|_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta},\ \|\xi\|_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi},\ |\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)|\ge\delta,\ \|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^1(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\}\), where \(g_0,q_0,\eta,\xi\) are the displayed residual functionals of \(P\). No restriction involving a supplied outcome code is imposed.
defs.def:gaussian-class: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}=\{P:E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0,\ |\theta_0|\le C_{\theta},\ |Y|\le C_q,\ \eta\perp X,\ \eta\sim N(0,\sigma^2),\ \|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g,\ \|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n},\ \|\bar q_n-q_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}\}\), with \(g_0,q_0,\eta,\xi\) given by their displayed residual definitions.

snapshot.stmt:
Fix the same deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\), its clipped pair \((\bar g_n,\bar q_n)\), and the same nested radii \((\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n})\) as external inputs to the two separate branches. Along every sequence of indices \(n\to\infty\) for which \(n\ge2\), \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\), and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\), the broad separated non-Gaussian branch satisfies
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\asymp n^{-1}.
\]
This includes fixed nonzero \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\); the witnessing statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\), as well as membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), imposes no restriction on and makes no use of \(\widehat q_n\), \(\bar q_n\), or \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\). Separately, every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in the simultaneous bounded-observed-outcome Gaussian intersection defined in \(\text{def:gaussian-class}\) satisfies \(\theta_0(P)=0\). Whenever that intersection is nonempty,
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}
 =\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}
 =0.
\]
Thus \(\text{prop:bounded-outcome-gaussian-degeneracy}\) diagnoses an incompatibility internal to the simultaneous exact-PLM, bounded-\(Y\), and nondegenerate conditional-Gaussian assumptions stated in Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Theorem 3.2. The positive lower-bound claim from that theorem is not relied upon here. No equality or inclusion between the two branches is asserted.

\]

\[

 =\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}
 =0.

snapshot.stmt:
The following two conclusions are valid, but they do not determine the full-class minimax phase diagram.

First, for each \(n\), let \(\mathcal C_n(\delta_n)\) be the class obtained from \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in \(\text{def:jms-ace-class}\) by replacing the fixed restriction \(\lvert\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)\rvert\ge\delta\) by \(\lvert\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)\rvert\ge\delta_n\), without changing any other restriction.  Define
\[
 \widetilde b_{2,n}
 =200\min\{1,C_{\theta}\}\delta_n
 \max\!\left\{
   \varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n},
   (\gamma n)^{-1/2}(\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta})
 \right\}^{-1}.
\]
Suppose \(\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n}>0\), all logarithms and denominators in the following display are defined, and the exact local eligibility condition
\[
 r\le
 \min\!\left\{
   \frac{b_{1,n}}{a_{1,n}}
   -\frac{1}{a_{1,n}}\log\!\left(\frac{b_{1,n}}{a_{1,n}}\right),
   \frac{\widetilde b_{2,n}}{a_2\log(a_2\widetilde b_{2,n})}
 \right\}
\]
holds.  Then the order-\(r\) ACE estimator obeys the local oracle benchmark
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{P\in\mathcal C_n(\delta_n)}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}
 \!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)\\
 &\quad\le
 C_{\gamma}r!16^r\delta_n^{-1}
 \Bigl[
   \varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
   +C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}\\
 &\hspace{42mm}
   +64(C_g+\psi_{\eta})^r
    \{r^2(C_g+\psi_{\eta})+\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta}\}
    (\gamma n)^{-1/2}
 \Bigr].
\end{aligned}
\]
Denote the right-hand side by \(U_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{loc}}\).  If \(U_{\mathrm{DML},n}\) denotes a separately valid ordinary-DML upper bound under its own hypotheses, then \(\min\{U_{\mathrm{DML},n},U_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{loc}}\}\) is only an oracle upper envelope; this comparison neither asserts a minimax rate nor constructs a data-driven selector.

Second, specialize to \(k=4\), hence \(r=3\).  For \(0<a\le1\), let
\[
 \eta_a=\sqrt{1-a^2}\,G_{\circ}+aS,
\]
where \(G_{\circ}\sim N(0,1)\), \(S\) is symmetric Rademacher, and \(G_{\circ}\perp S\).  Its moment generating function, fourth cumulant, and first positive characteristic zero are
\[
 M_a(z)=\exp\!\left(\frac{1-a^2}{2}z^2\right)\cosh(az),
 \qquad
 \kappa_4(\eta_a)=-2a^4,
 \qquad
 t_a=\frac{\pi}{2a}.
\]
For every real \(d\),
\[
 E\!\left[\sin\{t_a(\eta_a+d)\}\right]=0.
\]
Consider any law satisfying \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\), \(\eta=\eta_a\perp X\), \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\) almost surely, \(\lvert\theta_0(P)\rvert\le C_{\theta}\), \(\lVert g_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_g\), \(\lVert q_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_q\), \(\lVert\xi\rVert_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}\) almost surely, and \(\lVert\bar g_n-g_0\rVert_{L^1(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\).  Put
\[
 A_a=a\exp\!\left\{-\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{8a^2}\right\}.
\]
If \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le1/2\), then
\[
 E_P\!\left[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)\right]
 =A_aE_P[\cos(t_aD_n)]
 \ge\frac{A_a}{2}.
\]
Writing \(\mathbb P_n\) for the empirical average, define the computable clipped ratio
\[
 \widehat\theta_{a,n}
 =
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle
 \Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}
 \frac{\mathbb P_n[Y\sin(t_aZ_n)]}
      {\mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]},
 &\displaystyle
 \mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]\ge A_a/4,\\[3mm]
 0,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\]
There is a finite constant \(C\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), such that
\[
 \sup_P E_P\!\left[(\widehat\theta_{a,n}-\theta_0(P))^2\right]
 \le
 C\min\!\left\{
  1,\frac{1}{n}a^{-2}
  \exp\!\left(\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{4a^2}\right)
 \right\},
\]
where the supremum is over the just-displayed path laws.  Equivalently, with \(\Delta_a=2a^4=\lvert\kappa_4(\eta_a)\rvert\), the condition \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le1/2\) is
\[
 \varepsilon_{1,n}\le\frac{\Delta_a^{1/4}}{2^{1/4}\pi},
\]
and the preceding risk is at most
\[
 C\min\!\left\{
  1,\frac{1}{n}\Delta_a^{-1/2}
  \exp\!\left(\frac{\pi^2\sqrt2}{4}\Delta_a^{-1/2}\right)
 \right\}.
\]
This last display is a construction-specific upper bound with \(\varepsilon_{1,n}=O(\Delta_a^{1/4})\); it is not asserted to be sharp for the class specified only by a fourth-cumulant lower bound.

snapshot.stmt: There is \(A_k<\infty\), depending only on \(k\), such that every centered law with \(\|\eta\|_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta}\) and \(|\kappa_k(\eta)|\ge\delta\) has a zero of \(M\) in \(\{|z|\le R_0\}\), where \(R_0\le A_k(\psi_{\eta}^2/\delta)^{1/(k-2)}\).

snapshot.stmt:
There exist a once-for-all deterministic witness bank satisfying \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\) and constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, after that one bank is fixed, the constants depend only on \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) and the associated statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) in \(\text{def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\) is a measurable sample map for which the following holds. \[
 \frac cn\le\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}
 \le\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le\frac Cn.
\]
This is an existence-level fixed-bank minimax result: no algorithm for obtaining the selected bank, its radii, or \(a_{\star}\) from the observations and displayed class constants is asserted.  After the selected bank is fixed, the statistic uses \(\bar g_n\), uses no supplied outcome code, and does not know the law of \(\eta\).  Its MSE bound implies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)
 \le\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}.
\]
No inclusion of the broad class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is asserted; the finite-order ACE comparison is confined to the separately defined subclass \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\).

snapshot.stmt:
The following conclusions are separate facts on separately defined, incomparable classes.  Fix the same deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\), its clipped pair \((\bar g_n,\bar q_n)\), and the same nested radii \((\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n})\) as external inputs.  Select and fix the one once-for-all witness bank whose existence is asserted in \(\text{thm:adaptive-rootn-minimax}\) using \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\).  Along every sequence of indices \(n\to\infty\) for which \(n\ge2\), \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\), and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\), the broad fixed-separated non-Gaussian class has the existence-level fixed-bank rate
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\asymp n^{-1}.
\]
This includes fixed nonzero \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\).  Conditional on that selected bank, the witnessing statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\), as well as membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), imposes no restriction on and makes no use of \(\widehat q_n\), \(\bar q_n\), or \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\); no effective construction of the bank is asserted.  Separately, every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in the simultaneous bounded-observed-outcome Gaussian intersection defined in \(\text{def:gaussian-class}\) satisfies \(\theta_0(P)=0\).  Whenever that intersection is nonempty,
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}
 =\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}
 =0.
\]
Thus \(\text{prop:bounded-outcome-gaussian-degeneracy}\) diagnoses an incompatibility internal to the simultaneous exact-PLM, bounded-\(Y\), and nondegenerate conditional-Gaussian assumptions stated in Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Theorem 3.2.  The positive lower-bound claim from that theorem is not relied upon here.  These facts do not constitute a Gaussian-versus-non-Gaussian minimax dichotomy or a local-to-Gaussian frontier, and no equality or inclusion between the two classes is asserted.

defs.def:contour-bank-handle:
The displayed fixed primitive constants are supplied by standard certified-real names: each is accompanied by nested rational intervals with widths tending effectively to zero and with the named real in every interval.  Use the exact Luxemburg convention in \(\text{ass:eta-subgaussian}\), and put
\[

      {\log(R_{\mathrm{out}}/R_{\mathrm{fac}})}.
\]

\[

 \{R_0+1/4+q2^{-m}:q\in\mathbb Z,\ 0\le q2^{-m}\le1/2\}.
\]
Let \(m_{\star}\) be the least \(m\ge3\) for which \(|\mathcal Q_m|>N_{\mathrm{cert}}\), enumerate \(\mathcal Q_{m_{\star}}\) increasingly as \(\rho_1<\cdots<\rho_J\), and set
\[

 \qquad

\]
\[

 \exp\{-4(\Lambda_{\star}-1)\psi_{\eta}^2R_{\mathrm{fac}}^2\}
 \left(\frac{h_{\star}}{R_{\mathrm{fac}}+R_1}\right)^{N_{\mathrm{cert}}}.
\]

defs.def:adaptive-contour-estimator:
Form the translated-dyadic bank and the rational certificate \(a_{\star}\) in \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\), and form \(\widehat F_{a,n}\) and \(\widehat G_{a,n}\) on the deterministic split \(I_a\).  All contour computations use the fixed parameterization \(z=\rho_je^{it}\), \(0\le t\le2\pi\), outward-rounded rational interval arithmetic, and deterministic uniform angular meshes.

For each fold and circle, bound the angular Lipschitz constant of \(|\widehat F_{a,n}(\rho_je^{it})|\) by
\[
 L^F_{aj}=\rho_j\sup_{z\in C_j}|\widehat F'_{a,n}(z)|
 \le \rho_j|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}|Z_{n,i}|e^{\rho_j|Z_{n,i}|}.
\]
Use a finite mesh whose mesh contribution is at most \(a_{\star}/128\).  At every node refine the outward modulus enclosure until its width is at most \(a_{\star}/128\).  The resulting certified interval for \(\inf_{C_j}|\widehat F_{a,n}|\) therefore has total width at most \(a_{\star}/64\).

Whenever the certified lower modulus \(m>0\), compute the winding integral using
\[
 W(t)=\rho_je^{it}\frac{\widehat F'_{0,n}(\rho_je^{it})}
                              {\widehat F_{0,n}(\rho_je^{it})}.
\]
The observable derivative sums for \(\widehat F'_{0,n}\) and \(\widehat F''_{0,n}\), together with \(m\), give
\[
 |W'(t)|\le
 \rho_j\frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F'_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_j^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F''_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F'_{0,n}|^2}{m^2}
 \right\}.
\]
Refine until the sum of deterministic quadrature and outward node-evaluation errors is strictly less than \(1/4\).  Set \(\widehat N_{0j,n}\) to the unique nonnegative integer certified by that enclosure; if there is none, declare the circle inadmissible.

Declare \(j\) pilot-admissible when its certified lower modulus is at least \(a_{\star}/2\) and \(\widehat N_{0j,n}\ge1\).  Let \(\widehat j_n\) be the smallest index among the admissible maximizers of the certified lower modulus.  Return zero if no index is admissible or if the evaluation-fold certified lower modulus on \(C_{\widehat j_n}\) is below \(a_{\star}/4\).

Otherwise put
\[
 V(t)=\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it}
 \frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it})}
      {\widehat F_{1,n}(\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it})}.
\]
The observable derivative sums for \(\widehat F'_{1,n}\), \(\widehat G_{1,n}\), and \(\widehat G'_{1,n}\), together with the certified positive denominator, give
\[
 |V'(t)|\le
 \rho_{\widehat j_n}\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_{\widehat j_n}^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup|\widehat G'_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|\sup|\widehat F'_{1,n}|}{m^2}
 \right\}.
\]
The final enclosure targets exactly
\[
 \frac{1}{2\pi\widehat N_{0\widehat j_n,n}}
 \int_0^{2\pi}V(t)\,dt.
\]
Refine this single complex interval enclosure until its radius is at most \(1/n\).  Its one rational midpoint has complex error at most \(1/n\) and is the sole numerical output before taking the real part and projecting onto \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\).  Certified positive denominators make every displayed Lipschitz bound finite; positive rational target widths make every refinement terminate.  Finite sums, interval refinements, deterministic tie-breaking, projection, and fallback are Borel measurable.  Under the certified-real input convention this defines a total measurable statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) computable from the sample and the supplied primitive-constant names.  It uses \(\bar g_n\), uses no supplied outcome code, and does not know the law of \(\eta\).

The following conclusions are separate facts on separately defined, incomparable classes.  Fix the same deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\), its clipped pair \((\bar g_n,\bar q_n)\), and the same nested radii \((\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n})\) as external inputs. \[

\]

\[

 =\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}
 =0.
\]

These facts do not constitute a Gaussian-versus-non-Gaussian minimax dichotomy or a local-to-Gaussian frontier, and no equality or inclusion between the two classes is asserted.

defs.def:contour-bank-handle:
The displayed fixed primitive constants are supplied by standard certified-real names: each is accompanied by nested rational intervals with widths tending effectively to zero and with the named real in every interval.  Use the exact Luxemburg convention in \(\text{ass:eta-subgaussian}\), and put
\[
 R_{\mathrm{fac}}=R_1+1,
 \qquad R_{\mathrm{out}}=R_{\mathrm{fac}}+1,
 \qquad
 Q_{\star}=
 \frac{4\psi_{\eta}^2R_{\mathrm{out}}^2}
      {\log(R_{\mathrm{out}}/R_{\mathrm{fac}})}.
\]
By terminating outward interval refinement, precompute an integer \(N_{\mathrm{cert}}\ge Q_{\star}\).  For \(m\ge3\), define the translated-dyadic grid
\[
 \mathcal Q_m=
 \{R_0+1/4+q2^{-m}:q\in\mathbb Z,\ 0\le q2^{-m}\le1/2\}.
\]
Let \(m_{\star}\) be the least \(m\ge3\) for which \(|\mathcal Q_m|>N_{\mathrm{cert}}\), enumerate \(\mathcal Q_{m_{\star}}\) increasingly as \(\rho_1<\cdots<\rho_J\), and set
\[
 d_{\star}=2^{-m_{\star}},\qquad h_{\star}=d_{\star}/3,
 \qquad
 \Lambda_{\star}=\frac{R_{\mathrm{fac}}+R_1}{R_{\mathrm{fac}}-R_1},
\]
\[
 a_{\mathrm{an}}=
 \exp\{-4(\Lambda_{\star}-1)\psi_{\eta}^2R_{\mathrm{fac}}^2\}
 \left(\frac{h_{\star}}{R_{\mathrm{fac}}+R_1}\right)^{N_{\mathrm{cert}}}.
\]
Again by terminating outward interval refinement, precompute a positive dyadic rational \(a_{\star}\le a_{\mathrm{an}}\).  The circles \(C_j=\{z:|z|=\rho_j\}\) form the once-for-all translated-dyadic contour bank.  The analytic boundary lower bound is \(a_{\mathrm{an}}\), while every selector threshold and numerical error budget uses the rational certificate \(a_{\star}\).  The bank and certificates are effective from the certified-real names of \((k,\delta,\psi_{\eta},R_0,R_1)\) through the displayed arithmetic and terminating finite searches.  The construction does not use the unknown law of \(\eta\).

snapshot.stmt:
There exist a once-for-all deterministic witness bank satisfying \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\) and constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, after that one bank is fixed, the constants depend only on \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) and the associated statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) in \(\text{def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\) is a measurable sample map for which the following holds.  For every \(n\ge2\) such that \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\) and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\),
\[
 \frac cn\le\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}
 \le\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le\frac Cn.
\]
This is an existence-level fixed-bank minimax result: no algorithm for obtaining the selected bank, its radii, or \(a_{\star}\) from the observations and displayed class constants is asserted.  After the selected bank is fixed, the statistic uses \(\bar g_n\), uses no supplied outcome code, and does not know the law of \(\eta\).  Its MSE bound implies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)
 \le\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}.
\]
No inclusion of the broad class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is asserted; the finite-order ACE comparison is confined to the separately defined subclass \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\).

defs.def:ace-comparison-subclass: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}=\{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}:\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n},\ \|\bar q_n-q_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}\}\). Thus this comparison class restores both supplied-code restrictions while retaining every condition of the broad spectral class.
defs.def:adaptive-contour-estimator:
Form the translated-dyadic bank and the rational certificate \(a_{\star}\) in \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\), and form \(\widehat F_{a,n}\) and \(\widehat G_{a,n}\) on the deterministic split \(I_a\).  All contour computations use the fixed parameterization \(z=\rho_je^{it}\), \(0\le t\le2\pi\), outward-rounded rational interval arithmetic, and deterministic uniform angular meshes.

For each fold and circle, bound the angular Lipschitz constant of \(|\widehat F_{a,n}(\rho_je^{it})|\) by
\[
 L^F_{aj}=\rho_j\sup_{z\in C_j}|\widehat F'_{a,n}(z)|
 \le \rho_j|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}|Z_{n,i}|e^{\rho_j|Z_{n,i}|}.
\]
Use a finite mesh whose mesh contribution is at most \(a_{\star}/128\).  At every node refine the outward modulus enclosure until its width is at most \(a_{\star}/128\).  The resulting certified interval for \(\inf_{C_j}|\widehat F_{a,n}|\) therefore has total width at most \(a_{\star}/64\).

Whenever the certified lower modulus \(m>0\), compute the winding integral using
\[
 W(t)=\rho_je^{it}\frac{\widehat F'_{0,n}(\rho_je^{it})}
                              {\widehat F_{0,n}(\rho_je^{it})}.
\]
The observable derivative sums for \(\widehat F'_{0,n}\) and \(\widehat F''_{0,n}\), together with \(m\), give
\[
 |W'(t)|\le
 \rho_j\frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F'_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_j^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F''_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F'_{0,n}|^2}{m^2}
 \right\}.
\]
Refine until the sum of deterministic quadrature and outward node-evaluation errors is strictly less than \(1/4\).  Set \(\widehat N_{0j,n}\) to the unique nonnegative integer certified by that enclosure; if there is none, declare the circle inadmissible.

Declare \(j\) pilot-admissible when its certified lower modulus is at least \(a_{\star}/2\) and \(\widehat N_{0j,n}\ge1\).  Let \(\widehat j_n\) be the smallest index among the admissible maximizers of the certified lower modulus.  Return zero if no index is admissible or if the evaluation-fold certified lower modulus on \(C_{\widehat j_n}\) is below \(a_{\star}/4\).

Otherwise put
\[
 V(t)=\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it}
 \frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it})}
      {\widehat F_{1,n}(\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it})}.
\]
The observable derivative sums for \(\widehat F'_{1,n}\), \(\widehat G_{1,n}\), and \(\widehat G'_{1,n}\), together with the certified positive denominator, give
\[
 |V'(t)|\le
 \rho_{\widehat j_n}\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_{\widehat j_n}^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup|\widehat G'_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|\sup|\widehat F'_{1,n}|}{m^2}
 \right\}.
\]
The final enclosure targets exactly
\[
 \frac{1}{2\pi\widehat N_{0\widehat j_n,n}}
 \int_0^{2\pi}V(t)\,dt.
\]
Refine this single complex interval enclosure until its radius is at most \(1/n\).  Its one rational midpoint has complex error at most \(1/n\) and is the sole numerical output before taking the real part and projecting onto \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\).  Certified positive denominators make every displayed Lipschitz bound finite; positive rational target widths make every refinement terminate.  Finite sums, interval refinements, deterministic tie-breaking, projection, and fallback are Borel measurable.  Under the certified-real input convention this defines a total measurable statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) computable from the sample and the supplied primitive-constant names.  It uses \(\bar g_n\), uses no supplied outcome code, and does not know the law of \(\eta\).

snapshot.stmt:
The following conclusions are separate facts on separately defined, incomparable classes.  Fix the same deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\), its clipped pair \((\bar g_n,\bar q_n)\), and the same nested radii \((\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n})\) as external inputs.  Select and fix the one once-for-all witness bank whose existence is asserted in \(\text{thm:adaptive-rootn-minimax}\) using \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\).  Along every sequence of indices \(n\to\infty\) for which \(n\ge2\), \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\), and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\), the broad fixed-separated non-Gaussian class has the existence-level fixed-bank rate
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\asymp n^{-1}.
\]
This includes fixed nonzero \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\).  Conditional on that selected bank, the witnessing statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\), as well as membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), imposes no restriction on and makes no use of \(\widehat q_n\), \(\bar q_n\), or \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\); no effective construction of the bank is asserted.  Separately, every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in the simultaneous bounded-observed-outcome Gaussian intersection defined in \(\text{def:gaussian-class}\) satisfies \(\theta_0(P)=0\).  Whenever that intersection is nonempty,
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}
 =\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}
 =0.
\]
Thus \(\text{prop:bounded-outcome-gaussian-degeneracy}\) diagnoses an incompatibility internal to the simultaneous exact-PLM, bounded-\(Y\), and nondegenerate conditional-Gaussian assumptions stated in Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Theorem 3.2.  The positive lower-bound claim from that theorem is not relied upon here.  These facts do not constitute a Gaussian-versus-non-Gaussian minimax dichotomy or a local-to-Gaussian frontier, and no equality or inclusion between the two classes is asserted.

defs.def:adaptive-contour-estimator:
Form the translated-dyadic bank and the rational certificate \(a_{\star}\) in \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\), and form \(\widehat F_{a,n}\) and \(\widehat G_{a,n}\) on the deterministic split \(I_a\).  All contour computations use the fixed parameterization \(z=\rho_je^{it}\), \(0\le t\le2\pi\), outward-rounded rational interval arithmetic, and deterministic uniform angular meshes.

For each fold and circle, bound the angular Lipschitz constant of \(|\widehat F_{a,n}(\rho_je^{it})|\) by
\[
 L^F_{aj}=\rho_j\sup_{z\in C_j}|\widehat F'_{a,n}(z)|
 \le \rho_j|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}|Z_{n,i}|e^{\rho_j|Z_{n,i}|}.
\]
Use a finite mesh whose mesh contribution is at most \(a_{\star}/128\).  At every node refine the outward modulus enclosure until its width is at most \(a_{\star}/128\).  The resulting certified interval for \(\inf_{C_j}|\widehat F_{a,n}|\) therefore has total width at most \(a_{\star}/64\).

Whenever the certified lower modulus \(m>0\), compute the winding integral using
\[
 W(t)=\rho_je^{it}\frac{\widehat F'_{0,n}(\rho_je^{it})}
                              {\widehat F_{0,n}(\rho_je^{it})}.
\]
The observable derivative sums for \(\widehat F'_{0,n}\) and \(\widehat F''_{0,n}\), together with \(m\), give
\[
 |W'(t)|\le
 \rho_j\frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F'_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_j^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F''_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F'_{0,n}|^2}{m^2}
 \right\}.
\]
Refine until the sum of deterministic quadrature and outward node-evaluation errors is strictly less than \(1/4\).  Set \(\widehat N_{0j,n}\) to the unique nonnegative integer certified by that enclosure; if there is none, declare the circle inadmissible.

Declare \(j\) pilot-admissible when its certified lower modulus is at least \(a_{\star}/2\) and \(\widehat N_{0j,n}\ge1\).  Let \(\widehat j_n\) be the smallest index among the admissible maximizers of the certified lower modulus.  Return zero if no index is admissible or if the evaluation-fold certified lower modulus on \(C_{\widehat j_n}\) is below \(a_{\star}/4\).

Otherwise put
\[
 V(t)=\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it}
 \frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it})}
      {\widehat F_{1,n}(\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it})}.
\]
The observable derivative sums for \(\widehat F'_{1,n}\), \(\widehat G_{1,n}\), and \(\widehat G'_{1,n}\), together with the certified positive denominator, give
\[
 |V'(t)|\le
 \rho_{\widehat j_n}\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_{\widehat j_n}^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup|\widehat G'_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|\sup|\widehat F'_{1,n}|}{m^2}
 \right\}.
\]
The final enclosure targets exactly
\[
 \frac{1}{2\pi\widehat N_{0\widehat j_n,n}}
 \int_0^{2\pi}V(t)\,dt.
\]
Refine this single complex interval enclosure until its radius is at most \(1/n\).  Its one rational midpoint has complex error at most \(1/n\) and is the sole numerical output before taking the real part and projecting onto \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\).  Certified positive denominators make every displayed Lipschitz bound finite; positive rational target widths make every refinement terminate.  Finite sums, interval refinements, deterministic tie-breaking, projection, and fallback are Borel measurable.  Under the certified-real input convention this defines a total measurable statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) computable from the sample and the supplied primitive-constant names.  It uses \(\bar g_n\), uses no supplied outcome code, and does not know the law of \(\eta\).

snapshot.stmt:
The following conclusions are separate facts on separately defined, incomparable classes.  Fix the same deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\), its clipped pair \((\bar g_n,\bar q_n)\), and the same nested radii \((\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n})\) as external inputs. \[

\]

\[

 =\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}
 =0.
\]

These facts do not constitute a Gaussian-versus-non-Gaussian minimax dichotomy or a local-to-Gaussian frontier, and no equality or inclusion between the two classes is asserted.

\[

\]

defs.def:adaptive-contour-estimator:

All contour computations use the fixed parameterization \(z=\rho_je^{it}\), \(0\le t\le2\pi\), outward-rounded rational interval arithmetic, and deterministic uniform angular meshes.

For each fold and circle, bound the angular Lipschitz constant of \(|\widehat F_{a,n}(\rho_je^{it})|\) by
\[
 L^F_{aj}=\rho_j\sup_{z\in C_j}|\widehat F'_{a,n}(z)|
 \le \rho_j|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}|Z_{n,i}|e^{\rho_j|Z_{n,i}|}.
\]
Use a finite mesh whose mesh contribution is at most \(a_{\star}/128\).  At every node refine the outward modulus enclosure until its width is at most \(a_{\star}/128\).  The resulting certified interval for \(\inf_{C_j}|\widehat F_{a,n}|\) therefore has total width at most \(a_{\star}/64\).

Whenever the certified lower modulus \(m>0\), compute the winding integral using
\[

                              {\widehat F_{0,n}(\rho_je^{it})}.
\]

\[

 \rho_j\frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F'_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_j^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F''_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F'_{0,n}|^2}{m^2}
 \right\}.
\]

Declare \(j\) pilot-admissible when its certified lower modulus is at least \(a_{\star}/2\) and \(\widehat N_{0j,n}\ge1\). \[
 V(t)=\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it}
 \frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it})}
      {\widehat F_{1,n}(\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it})}.
\]
The observable derivative sums for \(\widehat F'_{1,n}\), \(\widehat G_{1,n}\), and \(\widehat G'_{1,n}\), together with the certified positive denominator, give
\[
 |V'(t)|\le
 \rho_{\widehat j_n}\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_{\widehat j_n}^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup|\widehat G'_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|\sup|\widehat F'_{1,n}|}{m^2}
 \right\}.
\]
The final enclosure targets exactly
\[
 \frac{1}{2\pi\widehat N_{0\widehat j_n,n}}
 \int_0^{2\pi}V(t)\,dt.
\]

Its one rational midpoint has complex error at most \(1/n\) and is the sole numerical output before taking the real part and projecting onto \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\). \[

Under the certified-real input convention of \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\), its terminating finite searches compute, from the displayed primitive class constants and without access to the unknown law of \(\eta\), a finite translated-dyadic bank \(C_j=\{z:|z|=\rho_j\}\), \(1\le j\le J\), with \(R_0<\rho_j<R_1\), and a positive dyadic rational \(a_{\star}\). Every treatment-noise transform represented in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) has some \(j\) such that \(N_{C_j}(M)\ge1\) and
\[
 \inf_{z\in C_j}|M(z)|\ge a_{\star}.
\]
The same computed bank and certificate work uniformly in \(n\).

defs.def:contour-bank-handle:
The displayed fixed primitive constants are supplied by standard certified-real names: each is accompanied by nested rational intervals with widths tending effectively to zero and with the named real in every interval.  Use the exact Luxemburg convention in \(\text{ass:eta-subgaussian}\), and put
\[
 R_{\mathrm{fac}}=R_1+1,
 \qquad R_{\mathrm{out}}=R_{\mathrm{fac}}+1,
 \qquad
 Q_{\star}=
 \frac{4\psi_{\eta}^2R_{\mathrm{out}}^2}
      {\log(R_{\mathrm{out}}/R_{\mathrm{fac}})}.
\]
By terminating outward interval refinement, precompute an integer \(N_{\mathrm{cert}}\ge Q_{\star}\).  For \(m\ge3\), define the translated-dyadic grid
\[
 \mathcal Q_m=
 \{R_0+1/4+q2^{-m}:q\in\mathbb Z,\ 0\le q2^{-m}\le1/2\}.
\]
Let \(m_{\star}\) be the least \(m\ge3\) for which \(|\mathcal Q_m|>N_{\mathrm{cert}}\), enumerate \(\mathcal Q_{m_{\star}}\) increasingly as \(\rho_1<\cdots<\rho_J\), and set
\[
 d_{\star}=2^{-m_{\star}},\qquad h_{\star}=d_{\star}/3,
 \qquad
 \Lambda_{\star}=\frac{R_{\mathrm{fac}}+R_1}{R_{\mathrm{fac}}-R_1},
\]
\[
 a_{\mathrm{an}}=
 \exp\{-4(\Lambda_{\star}-1)\psi_{\eta}^2R_{\mathrm{fac}}^2\}
 \left(\frac{h_{\star}}{R_{\mathrm{fac}}+R_1}\right)^{N_{\mathrm{cert}}}.
\]
Again by terminating outward interval refinement, precompute a positive dyadic rational \(a_{\star}\le a_{\mathrm{an}}\).  The circles \(C_j=\{z:|z|=\rho_j\}\) form the once-for-all translated-dyadic contour bank.  The analytic boundary lower bound is \(a_{\mathrm{an}}\), while every selector threshold and numerical error budget uses the rational certificate \(a_{\star}\).  The bank and certificates are effective from the certified-real names of \((k,\delta,\psi_{\eta},R_0,R_1)\) through the displayed arithmetic and terminating finite searches.  The construction does not use the unknown law of \(\eta\).
defs.def:non-gaussian-class: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}=\{P: \eta\perp X,\ E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0,\ |\theta_0|\le C_{\theta},\ \|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g,\ \|q_0\|_{\infty}\le C_q,\ \|\eta\|_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta},\ \|\xi\|_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi},\ |\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)|\ge\delta,\ \|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^1(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\}\), where \(g_0,q_0,\eta,\xi\) are the displayed residual functionals of \(P\). No restriction involving a supplied outcome code is imposed.

assumptions.ass:eta-subgaussian:
With the exact Luxemburg convention
\[
 \lVert W\rVert_{\psi_2}
 =\inf\{u>0:E_P[\exp(W^2/u^2)]\le2\},
\]
the treatment noise satisfies \(\lVert\eta\rVert_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta}\).

snapshot.stmt:
Under the certified-real input convention, \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) and \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\) compute once for all a deterministic translated-dyadic bank and a positive dyadic rational \(a_{\star}\) from the displayed primitive class constants, without access to the unknown law of \(\eta\). There are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), such that the associated total measurable certified statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) in \(\text{def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\) satisfies, for every \(n\ge2\) with \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\) and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\),
\[
 \frac cn\le\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}
 \le\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le\frac Cn.
\]
The statistic is a computable observed-sample map from the supplied certified-real names, uses \(\bar g_n\), uses no supplied outcome code, and does not know the law of \(\eta\). Its MSE bound implies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)
 \le\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}.
\]
No inclusion of the broad class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is asserted; the finite-order ACE comparison is confined to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\). The constants may deteriorate with fixed \(\delta\), and this theorem gives no useful shrinking-\(\delta_n\) rate, adaptive switching rule, or uniform inference result.

defs.def:ace-comparison-subclass: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}=\{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}:\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n},\ \|\bar q_n-q_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}\}\). Thus this comparison class restores both supplied-code restrictions while retaining every condition of the broad spectral class.
defs.def:adaptive-contour-estimator:
Form the translated-dyadic bank and the rational certificate \(a_{\star}\) in \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\), and form \(\widehat F_{a,n}\) and \(\widehat G_{a,n}\) on the deterministic split \(I_a\).  All contour computations use the fixed parameterization \(z=\rho_je^{it}\), \(0\le t\le2\pi\), outward-rounded rational interval arithmetic, and deterministic uniform angular meshes.

For each fold and circle, bound the angular Lipschitz constant of \(|\widehat F_{a,n}(\rho_je^{it})|\) by
\[
 L^F_{aj}=\rho_j\sup_{z\in C_j}|\widehat F'_{a,n}(z)|
 \le \rho_j|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}|Z_{n,i}|e^{\rho_j|Z_{n,i}|}.
\]
Use a finite mesh whose mesh contribution is at most \(a_{\star}/128\).  At every node refine the outward modulus enclosure until its width is at most \(a_{\star}/128\).  The resulting certified interval for \(\inf_{C_j}|\widehat F_{a,n}|\) therefore has total width at most \(a_{\star}/64\).

Whenever the certified lower modulus \(m>0\), compute the winding integral using
\[
 W(t)=\rho_je^{it}\frac{\widehat F'_{0,n}(\rho_je^{it})}
                              {\widehat F_{0,n}(\rho_je^{it})}.
\]
The observable derivative sums for \(\widehat F'_{0,n}\) and \(\widehat F''_{0,n}\), together with \(m\), give
\[
 |W'(t)|\le
 \rho_j\frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F'_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_j^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F''_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F'_{0,n}|^2}{m^2}
 \right\}.
\]
Refine until the sum of deterministic quadrature and outward node-evaluation errors is strictly less than \(1/4\).  Set \(\widehat N_{0j,n}\) to the unique nonnegative integer certified by that enclosure; if there is none, declare the circle inadmissible.

Declare \(j\) pilot-admissible when its certified lower modulus is at least \(a_{\star}/2\) and \(\widehat N_{0j,n}\ge1\).  Let \(\widehat j_n\) be the smallest index among the admissible maximizers of the certified lower modulus.  Return zero if no index is admissible or if the evaluation-fold certified lower modulus on \(C_{\widehat j_n}\) is below \(a_{\star}/4\).

Otherwise put
\[
 V(t)=\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it}
 \frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it})}
      {\widehat F_{1,n}(\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it})}.
\]
The observable derivative sums for \(\widehat F'_{1,n}\), \(\widehat G_{1,n}\), and \(\widehat G'_{1,n}\), together with the certified positive denominator, give
\[
 |V'(t)|\le
 \rho_{\widehat j_n}\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_{\widehat j_n}^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup|\widehat G'_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|\sup|\widehat F'_{1,n}|}{m^2}
 \right\}.
\]
The final enclosure targets exactly
\[
 \frac{1}{2\pi\widehat N_{0\widehat j_n,n}}
 \int_0^{2\pi}V(t)\,dt.
\]
Refine this single complex interval enclosure until its radius is at most \(1/n\).  Its one rational midpoint has complex error at most \(1/n\) and is the sole numerical output before taking the real part and projecting onto \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\).  Certified positive denominators make every displayed Lipschitz bound finite; positive rational target widths make every refinement terminate.  Finite sums, interval refinements, deterministic tie-breaking, projection, and fallback are Borel measurable.  Under the certified-real input convention this defines a total measurable statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) computable from the sample and the supplied primitive-constant names.  It uses \(\bar g_n\), uses no supplied outcome code, and does not know the law of \(\eta\).

snapshot.stmt:
The following are separate facts on separately defined, incomparable classes. Fix the same deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\), its clipped pair \((\bar g_n,\bar q_n)\), and the same nested radii \((\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n})\) as external inputs. Under the certified-real input convention, compute and fix the once-for-all translated-dyadic bank and positive dyadic certificate supplied by \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\). Along every sequence of indices \(n\to\infty\) for which \(n\ge2\), \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\), and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\),
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\asymp n^{-1}.
\]
This includes fixed nonzero \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\). The witnessing total certified statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\), as well as membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), imposes no restriction on and makes no use of \(\widehat q_n\), \(\bar q_n\), or \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\). Separately, every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in the simultaneous bounded-observed-outcome Gaussian intersection of \(\text{def:gaussian-class}\) satisfies \(\theta_0(P)=0\). Whenever that intersection is nonempty,
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}
 =\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}
 =0.
\]
Thus \(\text{prop:bounded-outcome-gaussian-degeneracy}\) is solely a diagnostic of the simultaneous exact-PLM, bounded-\(Y\), and nondegenerate conditional-Gaussian assumptions stated around Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Theorem 3.2; its positive lower-bound claim is not used. These conclusions neither form a Gaussian-versus-non-Gaussian minimax dichotomy nor determine a local-to-Gaussian frontier, and no equality or inclusion between the two classes is asserted.
