Under the certified-real input convention of \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\), its terminating finite searches compute, from the displayed primitive class constants and without access to the unknown law of \(\eta\), a finite translated-dyadic bank \(C_j=\{z:|z|=\rho_j\}\), \(1\le j\le J\), with \(R_0<\rho_j<R_1\), and a positive dyadic rational \(a_{\star}\). Every treatment-noise transform represented in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) has some \(j\) such that \(N_{C_j}(M)\ge1\) and
\[
 \inf_{z\in C_j}|M(z)|\ge a_{\star}.
\]
The same computed bank and certificate work uniformly in \(n\).

defs.def:contour-bank-handle:
The displayed fixed primitive constants are supplied by standard certified-real names: each is accompanied by nested rational intervals with widths tending effectively to zero and with the named real in every interval.  Use the exact Luxemburg convention in \(\text{ass:eta-subgaussian}\), and put
\[
 R_{\mathrm{fac}}=R_1+1,
 \qquad R_{\mathrm{out}}=R_{\mathrm{fac}}+1,
 \qquad
 Q_{\star}=
 \frac{4\psi_{\eta}^2R_{\mathrm{out}}^2}
      {\log(R_{\mathrm{out}}/R_{\mathrm{fac}})}.
\]
By terminating outward interval refinement, precompute an integer \(N_{\mathrm{cert}}\ge Q_{\star}\).  For \(m\ge3\), define the translated-dyadic grid
\[
 \mathcal Q_m=
 \{R_0+1/4+q2^{-m}:q\in\mathbb Z,\ 0\le q2^{-m}\le1/2\}.
\]
Let \(m_{\star}\) be the least \(m\ge3\) for which \(|\mathcal Q_m|>N_{\mathrm{cert}}\), enumerate \(\mathcal Q_{m_{\star}}\) increasingly as \(\rho_1<\cdots<\rho_J\), and set
\[
 d_{\star}=2^{-m_{\star}},\qquad h_{\star}=d_{\star}/3,
 \qquad
 \Lambda_{\star}=\frac{R_{\mathrm{fac}}+R_1}{R_{\mathrm{fac}}-R_1},
\]
\[
 a_{\mathrm{an}}=
 \exp\{-4(\Lambda_{\star}-1)\psi_{\eta}^2R_{\mathrm{fac}}^2\}
 \left(\frac{h_{\star}}{R_{\mathrm{fac}}+R_1}\right)^{N_{\mathrm{cert}}}.
\]
Again by terminating outward interval refinement, precompute a positive dyadic rational \(a_{\star}\le a_{\mathrm{an}}\).  The circles \(C_j=\{z:|z|=\rho_j\}\) form the once-for-all translated-dyadic contour bank.  The analytic boundary lower bound is \(a_{\mathrm{an}}\), while every selector threshold and numerical error budget uses the rational certificate \(a_{\star}\).  The bank and certificates are effective from the certified-real names of \((k,\delta,\psi_{\eta},R_0,R_1)\) through the displayed arithmetic and terminating finite searches.  The construction does not use the unknown law of \(\eta\).
defs.def:non-gaussian-class: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}=\{P: \eta\perp X,\ E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0,\ |\theta_0|\le C_{\theta},\ \|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g,\ \|q_0\|_{\infty}\le C_q,\ \|\eta\|_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta},\ \|\xi\|_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi},\ |\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)|\ge\delta,\ \|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^1(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\}\), where \(g_0,q_0,\eta,\xi\) are the displayed residual functionals of \(P\). No restriction involving a supplied outcome code is imposed.

assumptions.ass:eta-subgaussian:
With the exact Luxemburg convention
\[
 \lVert W\rVert_{\psi_2}
 =\inf\{u>0:E_P[\exp(W^2/u^2)]\le2\},
\]
the treatment noise satisfies \(\lVert\eta\rVert_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta}\).

snapshot.stmt:
Under the certified-real input convention, \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) and \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\) compute once for all a deterministic translated-dyadic bank and a positive dyadic rational \(a_{\star}\) from the displayed primitive class constants, without access to the unknown law of \(\eta\). There are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), such that the associated total measurable certified statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) in \(\text{def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\) satisfies, for every \(n\ge2\) with \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\) and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\),
\[
 \frac cn\le\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}
 \le\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le\frac Cn.
\]
The statistic is a computable observed-sample map from the supplied certified-real names, uses \(\bar g_n\), uses no supplied outcome code, and does not know the law of \(\eta\). Its MSE bound implies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)
 \le\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}.
\]
No inclusion of the broad class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is asserted; the finite-order ACE comparison is confined to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\). The constants may deteriorate with fixed \(\delta\), and this theorem gives no useful shrinking-\(\delta_n\) rate, adaptive switching rule, or uniform inference result.

defs.def:ace-comparison-subclass: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}=\{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}:\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n},\ \|\bar q_n-q_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}\}\). Thus this comparison class restores both supplied-code restrictions while retaining every condition of the broad spectral class.
defs.def:adaptive-contour-estimator:
Form the translated-dyadic bank and the rational certificate \(a_{\star}\) in \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\), and form \(\widehat F_{a,n}\) and \(\widehat G_{a,n}\) on the deterministic split \(I_a\).  All contour computations use the fixed parameterization \(z=\rho_je^{it}\), \(0\le t\le2\pi\), outward-rounded rational interval arithmetic, and deterministic uniform angular meshes.

For each fold and circle, bound the angular Lipschitz constant of \(|\widehat F_{a,n}(\rho_je^{it})|\) by
\[
 L^F_{aj}=\rho_j\sup_{z\in C_j}|\widehat F'_{a,n}(z)|
 \le \rho_j|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}|Z_{n,i}|e^{\rho_j|Z_{n,i}|}.
\]
Use a finite mesh whose mesh contribution is at most \(a_{\star}/128\).  At every node refine the outward modulus enclosure until its width is at most \(a_{\star}/128\).  The resulting certified interval for \(\inf_{C_j}|\widehat F_{a,n}|\) therefore has total width at most \(a_{\star}/64\).

Whenever the certified lower modulus \(m>0\), compute the winding integral using
\[
 W(t)=\rho_je^{it}\frac{\widehat F'_{0,n}(\rho_je^{it})}
                              {\widehat F_{0,n}(\rho_je^{it})}.
\]
The observable derivative sums for \(\widehat F'_{0,n}\) and \(\widehat F''_{0,n}\), together with \(m\), give
\[
 |W'(t)|\le
 \rho_j\frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F'_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_j^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F''_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F'_{0,n}|^2}{m^2}
 \right\}.
\]
Refine until the sum of deterministic quadrature and outward node-evaluation errors is strictly less than \(1/4\).  Set \(\widehat N_{0j,n}\) to the unique nonnegative integer certified by that enclosure; if there is none, declare the circle inadmissible.

Declare \(j\) pilot-admissible when its certified lower modulus is at least \(a_{\star}/2\) and \(\widehat N_{0j,n}\ge1\).  Let \(\widehat j_n\) be the smallest index among the admissible maximizers of the certified lower modulus.  Return zero if no index is admissible or if the evaluation-fold certified lower modulus on \(C_{\widehat j_n}\) is below \(a_{\star}/4\).

Otherwise put
\[
 V(t)=\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it}
 \frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it})}
      {\widehat F_{1,n}(\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it})}.
\]
The observable derivative sums for \(\widehat F'_{1,n}\), \(\widehat G_{1,n}\), and \(\widehat G'_{1,n}\), together with the certified positive denominator, give
\[
 |V'(t)|\le
 \rho_{\widehat j_n}\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_{\widehat j_n}^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup|\widehat G'_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|\sup|\widehat F'_{1,n}|}{m^2}
 \right\}.
\]
The final enclosure targets exactly
\[
 \frac{1}{2\pi\widehat N_{0\widehat j_n,n}}
 \int_0^{2\pi}V(t)\,dt.
\]
Refine this single complex interval enclosure until its radius is at most \(1/n\).  Its one rational midpoint has complex error at most \(1/n\) and is the sole numerical output before taking the real part and projecting onto \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\).  Certified positive denominators make every displayed Lipschitz bound finite; positive rational target widths make every refinement terminate.  Finite sums, interval refinements, deterministic tie-breaking, projection, and fallback are Borel measurable.  Under the certified-real input convention this defines a total measurable statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) computable from the sample and the supplied primitive-constant names.  It uses \(\bar g_n\), uses no supplied outcome code, and does not know the law of \(\eta\).

snapshot.stmt:
The following are separate facts on separately defined, incomparable classes. Fix the same deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\), its clipped pair \((\bar g_n,\bar q_n)\), and the same nested radii \((\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n})\) as external inputs. Under the certified-real input convention, compute and fix the once-for-all translated-dyadic bank and positive dyadic certificate supplied by \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\). Along every sequence of indices \(n\to\infty\) for which \(n\ge2\), \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\), and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\),
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\asymp n^{-1}.
\]
This includes fixed nonzero \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\). The witnessing total certified statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\), as well as membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), imposes no restriction on and makes no use of \(\widehat q_n\), \(\bar q_n\), or \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\). Separately, every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in the simultaneous bounded-observed-outcome Gaussian intersection of \(\text{def:gaussian-class}\) satisfies \(\theta_0(P)=0\). Whenever that intersection is nonempty,
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}
 =\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}
 =0.
\]
Thus \(\text{prop:bounded-outcome-gaussian-degeneracy}\) is solely a diagnostic of the simultaneous exact-PLM, bounded-\(Y\), and nondegenerate conditional-Gaussian assumptions stated around Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Theorem 3.2; its positive lower-bound claim is not used. These conclusions neither form a Gaussian-versus-non-Gaussian minimax dichotomy nor determine a local-to-Gaussian frontier, and no equality or inclusion between the two classes is asserted.

Under the certified-real input convention, \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) and \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\) compute once for all a deterministic translated-dyadic bank and a positive dyadic rational \(a_{\star}\) from the displayed primitive class constants, without access to the unknown law of \(\eta\). There are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), such that the associated total measurable certified statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) in \(\text{def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\) satisfies, for every \(n\ge2\) with \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\) and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\),
\[
 \frac cn\le\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}
 \le\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le\frac Cn.
\]
The statistic is a computable observed-sample map from the supplied certified-real names, uses \(\bar g_n\), uses no supplied outcome code, and does not know the law of \(\eta\). Its MSE bound implies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)
 \le\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}.
\]
No inclusion of the broad class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is asserted; the finite-order ACE comparison is confined to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\). The constants may deteriorate with fixed \(\delta\), and this theorem gives no useful shrinking-\(\delta_n\) rate, adaptive switching rule, or uniform inference result.

defs.def:ace-comparison-subclass: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}=\{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}:\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n},\ \|\bar q_n-q_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}\}\). Thus this comparison class restores both supplied-code restrictions while retaining every condition of the broad spectral class.
defs.def:adaptive-contour-estimator:
Use the following canonical representation convention.  For every observed real number \(x\), its input name is the unique nested dyadic name
\[
 \mathcal I_m(x)=
 \left[2^{-m}\lfloor2^m x\rfloor,
       2^{-m}\{\lfloor2^m x\rfloor+1\}\right],
 \qquad m\ge1.
\]
Thus the represented sample consists of the canonical names of \(T_i\), \(Y_i\), and \(\bar g_n(X_i)\), \(1\le i\le n\), together with the canonical certified names of the primitive constants.  The algorithm first invokes \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) internally on \((k,\delta,\psi_{\eta},R_0,R_1)\); it receives no externally chosen bank, contour diagnostics, empirical-transform names, or law-specific information.  It then constructs the canonical interval names of
\[
 Z_{n,i}=T_i-\bar g_n(X_i),
 \qquad
 \widehat F_{a,n}^{(p)}(z)
 =|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}Z_{n,i}^{p}e^{zZ_{n,i}},
 \quad p\in\{0,1,2\},
\]
and
\[
 \widehat G_{a,n}^{(p)}(z)
 =|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}Y_iZ_{n,i}^{p}e^{zZ_{n,i}},
 \quad p\in\{0,1\},
\]
by finite outward-rounded rational operations and the standard interval Taylor algorithm for the complex exponential.  In particular, \(\widehat F_{a,n}^{(0)}=\widehat F_{a,n}\) and \(\widehat G_{a,n}^{(0)}=\widehat G_{a,n}\).  These are derived names, not additional inputs.

All contour computations use \(z=\rho_je^{it}\), \(0\le t\le2\pi\), and deterministic uniform angular meshes.  For each fold and circle, the algorithm derives the certified upper bound
\[
 L^F_{aj}=\rho_j\sup_{z\in C_j}|\widehat F_{a,n}'(z)|
 \le \rho_j|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}|Z_{n,i}|e^{\rho_j|Z_{n,i}|}.
\]
It increases the mesh and the precision of every canonically derived node enclosure until the mesh error is at most \(a_{\star}/128\) and the aggregate node-enclosure error is at most \(a_{\star}/128\).  The minimum of the nodewise rational lower modulus endpoints minus the Lipschitz mesh allowance and the analogous upper endpoint form a canonical certified interval for \(\inf_{C_j}|\widehat F_{a,n}|\) of width at most \(a_{\star}/64\).

Whenever its certified lower endpoint \(m\) is positive, the algorithm derives enclosures of the actual winding integrand
\[
 W_{0j}(t)=
 \rho_je^{it}
 \frac{\widehat F'_{0,n}(\rho_je^{it})}
      {\widehat F_{0,n}(\rho_je^{it})}
\]
and uses the derived sums for \(\widehat F'_{0,n}\) and \(\widehat F''_{0,n}\) to certify
\[
 |W_{0j}'(t)|\le
 \rho_j\frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F'_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_j^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F''_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F'_{0,n}|^2}{m^2}
 \right\}.
\]
It refines the mesh and the canonically derived node enclosures until the outward enclosure of \((2\pi)^{-1}\int_0^{2\pi}W_{0j}(t)\,dt\) has radius strictly below \(1/4\).  If that enclosure contains a unique nonnegative integer, that integer is \(\widehat N_{0j,n}\); otherwise the circle is inadmissible.  Declare \(j\) pilot-admissible when its certified lower modulus endpoint is at least \(a_{\star}/2\) and \(\widehat N_{0j,n}\ge1\).  Let \(\widehat j_n\) be the smallest index among the admissible indices having maximal certified lower modulus endpoint.  Return zero if there is no such index.

On the evaluation fold, compute the same canonical modulus certificate on \(C_{\widehat j_n}\), and return zero if its lower endpoint is below \(a_{\star}/4\).  Otherwise the algorithm derives enclosures of the actual final contour integrand
\[
 V(t)=\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it}
 \frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it})}
      {\widehat F_{1,n}(\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it})}
\]
and the bound
\[
 |V'(t)|\le
 \rho_{\widehat j_n}\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_{\widehat j_n}^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup|\widehat G'_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|\sup|\widehat F'_{1,n}|}{m^2}
 \right\}.
\]
It refines until the canonical complex enclosure of
\[
 \frac{1}{2\pi\widehat N_{0\widehat j_n,n}}
 \int_0^{2\pi}V(t)\,dt
\]
has radius at most \(1/n\).  Its canonical rational midpoint is the sole numerical output before taking the real part and projecting onto \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\); the result is \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\).

An execution trace is the finite list of requested name precisions, mesh sizes, rational interval operations, rational comparisons, and branch decisions just described.  All threshold comparisons are comparisons of rational certified endpoints with the fixed rational thresholds, and every division is performed only after a positive rational denominator certificate.  The canonical-name convention makes the trace and output functions of the represented real values, not of arbitrary names.  The definition fixes the thresholds \(a_{\star}/2\) and \(a_{\star}/4\), the fallback zero, the smallest-index tie-break, and the final \(1/n\) error.  It uses \(\bar g_n\), uses no supplied outcome code, and has no access to the law of \(\eta\).  Termination, extensionality, and Borel measurability of this canonical algorithm are conclusions proved in \(\text{thm:adaptive-rootn-minimax}\), not assumptions of the definition.
defs.def:contour-bank-handle:
The certified-real convention is the following.  The integer \(k\) is given exactly, and each of the positive reals \(\delta,\psi_{\eta},R_0,R_1\) is supplied by its canonical nested dyadic enclosure name.  No transform, distribution, oracle, or sample-dependent object is an input.  Put
\[
 R_{\mathrm{fac}}=R_1+1,
 \qquad R_{\mathrm{out}}=R_{\mathrm{fac}}+1,
 \qquad
 Q_{\star}=
 \frac{4\psi_{\eta}^2R_{\mathrm{out}}^2}
      {\log(R_{\mathrm{out}}/R_{\mathrm{fac}})}.
\]
Refine outward intervals until the positive denominator in \(Q_{\star}\) has a positive rational lower endpoint and \(Q_{\star}\) has a finite rational upper endpoint \(U_{\star}\), and set \(N_{\mathrm{cert}}=\lceil U_{\star}\rceil\).  For \(m\ge3\), define
\[
 \mathcal Q_m=
 \{R_0+1/4+q2^{-m}:q\in\mathbb Z,\ 0\le q2^{-m}\le1/2\}.
\]
Let \(m_{\star}\) be the least \(m\ge3\) for which \(|\mathcal Q_m|>N_{\mathrm{cert}}\), enumerate \(\mathcal Q_{m_{\star}}\) increasingly as \(\rho_1<\cdots<\rho_J\), and set
\[
 d_{\star}=2^{-m_{\star}},\qquad h_{\star}=d_{\star}/3,
 \qquad
 \Lambda_{\star}=\frac{R_{\mathrm{fac}}+R_1}{R_{\mathrm{fac}}-R_1},
\]
\[
 a_{\mathrm{an}}=
 \exp\{-4(\Lambda_{\star}-1)\psi_{\eta}^2R_{\mathrm{fac}}^2\}
 \left(\frac{h_{\star}}{R_{\mathrm{fac}}+R_1}\right)^{N_{\mathrm{cert}}}.
\]
Refine an outward interval for \(a_{\mathrm{an}}\) until its rational lower endpoint \(L_{\star}\) is positive.  Let \(u_{\star}\ge1\) be the least integer with \(2^{-u_{\star}}\le L_{\star}\), and set \(a_{\star}=2^{-u_{\star}}\).  Set \(C_j=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=\rho_j\}\).  This is the once-for-all translated-dyadic bank.  Its construction inputs are exactly the certified primitive constants \((k,\delta,\psi_{\eta},R_0,R_1)\); the unknown law of \(\eta\) is not an input.  The universal guarantee for treatment-noise transforms is stated and proved separately in \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\).
defs.def:minimax-risks: \(\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}=\inf_{\widetilde\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_n;\bar g_n,\bar q_n)}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}E_P[(\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P))^2]\), \(\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}=\inf_{\widetilde\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_n;\bar g_n,\bar q_n)}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}E_P[(\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P))^2]\), and \(\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}=\inf_{\widetilde\theta}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P)|)\).
defs.def:non-gaussian-class: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}=\{P: \eta\perp X,\ E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0,\ |\theta_0|\le C_{\theta},\ \|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g,\ \|q_0\|_{\infty}\le C_q,\ \|\eta\|_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta},\ \|\xi\|_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi},\ |\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)|\ge\delta,\ \|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^1(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\}\), where \(g_0,q_0,\eta,\xi\) are the displayed residual functionals of \(P\). defs.def:gaussian-class: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}=\{P:E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0,\ |\theta_0|\le C_{\theta},\ |Y|\le C_q,\ \eta\perp X,\ \eta\sim N(0,\sigma^2),\ \|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g,\ \|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n},\ \|\bar q_n-q_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}\}\), with \(g_0,q_0,\eta,\xi\) given by their displayed residual definitions.

 =\inf\{u>0:E_P[\exp(W^2/u^2)]\le2\},
\]
the treatment noise satisfies \(\lVert\eta\rVert_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta}\).

defs.def:jms-eligibility: Compute \(a_{1,n},b_{1,n},a_2,b_{2,n}\) exactly as in condition (21) and set \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) to the condition \(r\le\min\{b_{1,n}/a_{1,n}-a_{1,n}^{-1}\log(b_{1,n}/a_{1,n}),b_{2,n}/[a_2\log(a_2b_{2,n})]\}\) on indices for which these expressions are defined.
defs.def:non-gaussian-class: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}=\{P: \eta\perp X,\ E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0,\ |\theta_0|\le C_{\theta},\ \|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g,\ \|q_0\|_{\infty}\le C_q,\ \|\eta\|_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta},\ \|\xi\|_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi},\ |\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)|\ge\delta,\ \|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^1(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\}\), where \(g_0,q_0,\eta,\xi\) are the displayed residual functionals of \(P\). If \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\), then it contains a one-dimensional submodel \(\{P_{n,\vartheta}:|\vartheta|\le c_0\}\) with the same law of \((X,T)\), the same \(g_0,q_0,\bar g_n,\bar q_n\), independent Gaussian outcome innovation of fixed positive variance not exceeding the \(\psi_{\xi}\) envelope, and \(Y_{\vartheta}=q_0(X)+\vartheta\eta+\xi_{\star}\). Under the certified-real input convention, \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) and \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\) compute once for all a deterministic translated-dyadic bank and a positive dyadic rational \(a_{\star}\) from the displayed primitive class constants, without access to the unknown law of \(\eta\). There are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), such that the associated total measurable certified statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) in \(\text{def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\) satisfies, for every \(n\ge2\) with \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\) and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\),
\[
 \frac cn\le\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}
 \le\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le\frac Cn.
\]
The statistic is a computable observed-sample map from the supplied certified-real names, uses \(\bar g_n\), uses no supplied outcome code, and does not know the law of \(\eta\). Its MSE bound implies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)
 \le\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}.
\]
Moreover, \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\). Hence, whenever \(n\ge2\), \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\), and \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\neq\varnothing\),
\[
 \frac cn
 \le
 \inf_{\widetilde\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_n;\bar g_n,\bar q_n)}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 E_P[(\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le\frac Cn,
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)
 \le\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}.
\]
No inclusion \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is asserted. The finite-order ACE and spectral generalized-quantile guarantees may therefore be compared on the full published ACE class, and that class itself has matched \(\Theta(n^{-1})\) minimax mean-squared error. The latter lower bound is over all estimators on the class; it is not a lower bound on \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}\) or on its cited generalized-quantile guarantee. The class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) remains the additional \(L^s(P_X)\)-restricted subclass and equals the published ACE class when \(s=r\) under the common clipped-code convention. The constants may deteriorate with fixed \(\delta\), and this theorem gives no useful shrinking-\(\delta_n\) rate, adaptive switching rule, uniform inference result, or matching local lower bound.

defs.def:adaptive-contour-estimator:
Use the following canonical representation convention.  For every observed real number \(x\), its input name is the unique nested dyadic name
\[
 \mathcal I_m(x)=
 \left[2^{-m}\lfloor2^m x\rfloor,
       2^{-m}\{\lfloor2^m x\rfloor+1\}\right],
 \qquad m\ge1.
\]
Thus the represented sample consists of the canonical names of \(T_i\), \(Y_i\), and \(\bar g_n(X_i)\), \(1\le i\le n\), together with the canonical certified names of the primitive constants.  The algorithm first invokes \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) internally on \((k,\delta,\psi_{\eta},R_0,R_1)\); it receives no externally chosen bank, contour diagnostics, empirical-transform names, or law-specific information.  It then constructs the canonical interval names of
\[
 Z_{n,i}=T_i-\bar g_n(X_i),
 \qquad
 \widehat F_{a,n}^{(p)}(z)
 =|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}Z_{n,i}^{p}e^{zZ_{n,i}},
 \quad p\in\{0,1,2\},
\]
and
\[
 \widehat G_{a,n}^{(p)}(z)
 =|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}Y_iZ_{n,i}^{p}e^{zZ_{n,i}},
 \quad p\in\{0,1\},
\]
by finite outward-rounded rational operations and the standard interval Taylor algorithm for the complex exponential.  In particular, \(\widehat F_{a,n}^{(0)}=\widehat F_{a,n}\) and \(\widehat G_{a,n}^{(0)}=\widehat G_{a,n}\).  These are derived names, not additional inputs.

All contour computations use \(z=\rho_je^{it}\), \(0\le t\le2\pi\), and deterministic uniform angular meshes.  For each fold and circle, the algorithm derives the certified upper bound
\[
 L^F_{aj}=\rho_j\sup_{z\in C_j}|\widehat F_{a,n}'(z)|
 \le \rho_j|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}|Z_{n,i}|e^{\rho_j|Z_{n,i}|}.
\]
It increases the mesh and the precision of every canonically derived node enclosure until the mesh error is at most \(a_{\star}/128\) and the aggregate node-enclosure error is at most \(a_{\star}/128\).  The minimum of the nodewise rational lower modulus endpoints minus the Lipschitz mesh allowance and the analogous upper endpoint form a canonical certified interval for \(\inf_{C_j}|\widehat F_{a,n}|\) of width at most \(a_{\star}/64\).

Whenever its certified lower endpoint \(m\) is positive, the algorithm derives enclosures of the actual winding integrand
\[
 W_{0j}(t)=
 \rho_je^{it}
 \frac{\widehat F'_{0,n}(\rho_je^{it})}
      {\widehat F_{0,n}(\rho_je^{it})}
\]
and uses the derived sums for \(\widehat F'_{0,n}\) and \(\widehat F''_{0,n}\) to certify
\[
 |W_{0j}'(t)|\le
 \rho_j\frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F'_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_j^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F''_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F'_{0,n}|^2}{m^2}
 \right\}.
\]
It refines the mesh and the canonically derived node enclosures until the outward enclosure of \((2\pi)^{-1}\int_0^{2\pi}W_{0j}(t)\,dt\) has radius strictly below \(1/4\).  If that enclosure contains a unique nonnegative integer, that integer is \(\widehat N_{0j,n}\); otherwise the circle is inadmissible.  Declare \(j\) pilot-admissible when its certified lower modulus endpoint is at least \(a_{\star}/2\) and \(\widehat N_{0j,n}\ge1\).  Let \(\widehat j_n\) be the smallest index among the admissible indices having maximal certified lower modulus endpoint.  Return zero if there is no such index.

On the evaluation fold, compute the same canonical modulus certificate on \(C_{\widehat j_n}\), and return zero if its lower endpoint is below \(a_{\star}/4\).  Otherwise the algorithm derives enclosures of the actual final contour integrand
\[
 V(t)=\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it}
 \frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it})}
      {\widehat F_{1,n}(\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it})}
\]
and the bound
\[
 |V'(t)|\le
 \rho_{\widehat j_n}\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_{\widehat j_n}^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup|\widehat G'_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|\sup|\widehat F'_{1,n}|}{m^2}
 \right\}.
\]
It refines until the canonical complex enclosure of
\[
 \frac{1}{2\pi\widehat N_{0\widehat j_n,n}}
 \int_0^{2\pi}V(t)\,dt
\]
has radius at most \(1/n\).  Its canonical rational midpoint is the sole numerical output before taking the real part and projecting onto \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\); the result is \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\).

An execution trace is the finite list of requested name precisions, mesh sizes, rational interval operations, rational comparisons, and branch decisions just described.  All threshold comparisons are comparisons of rational certified endpoints with the fixed rational thresholds, and every division is performed only after a positive rational denominator certificate.  The canonical-name convention makes the trace and output functions of the represented real values, not of arbitrary names.  The definition fixes the thresholds \(a_{\star}/2\) and \(a_{\star}/4\), the fallback zero, the smallest-index tie-break, and the final \(1/n\) error.  It uses \(\bar g_n\), uses no supplied outcome code, and has no access to the law of \(\eta\).  Termination, extensionality, and Borel measurability of this canonical algorithm are conclusions proved in \(\text{thm:adaptive-rootn-minimax}\), not assumptions of the definition.

defs.def:contour-bank-handle:

 \left(\frac{h_{\star}}{R_{\mathrm{fac}}+R_1}\right)^{N_{\mathrm{cert}}}.

defs.def:adaptive-contour-estimator:
Use the following canonical representation convention.  For every observed real number \(x\), its input name is the unique nested dyadic name
\[
 \mathcal I_m(x)=
 \left[2^{-m}\lfloor2^m x\rfloor,
       2^{-m}\{\lfloor2^m x\rfloor+1\}\right],
 \qquad m\ge1.
\]
Thus the represented sample consists of the canonical names of \(T_i\), \(Y_i\), and \(\bar g_n(X_i)\), \(1\le i\le n\), together with the canonical certified names of the primitive constants.  The algorithm first invokes \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) internally on \((k,\delta,\psi_{\eta},R_0,R_1)\); it receives no externally chosen bank, contour diagnostics, empirical-transform names, or law-specific information.  It then constructs the canonical interval names of
\[
 Z_{n,i}=T_i-\bar g_n(X_i),
 \qquad
 \widehat F_{a,n}^{(p)}(z)
 =|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}Z_{n,i}^{p}e^{zZ_{n,i}},
 \quad p\in\{0,1,2\},
\]
and
\[
 \widehat G_{a,n}^{(p)}(z)
 =|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}Y_iZ_{n,i}^{p}e^{zZ_{n,i}},
 \quad p\in\{0,1\},
\]
by finite outward-rounded rational operations and the standard interval Taylor algorithm for the complex exponential.  In particular, \(\widehat F_{a,n}^{(0)}=\widehat F_{a,n}\) and \(\widehat G_{a,n}^{(0)}=\widehat G_{a,n}\).  These are derived names, not additional inputs.

All contour computations use \(z=\rho_je^{it}\), \(0\le t\le2\pi\), and deterministic uniform angular meshes.  For each fold and circle, the algorithm derives the certified upper bound
\[
 L^F_{aj}=\rho_j\sup_{z\in C_j}|\widehat F_{a,n}'(z)|
 \le \rho_j|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}|Z_{n,i}|e^{\rho_j|Z_{n,i}|}.
\]
It increases the mesh and the precision of every canonically derived node enclosure until the mesh error is at most \(a_{\star}/128\) and the aggregate node-enclosure error is at most \(a_{\star}/128\).  The minimum of the nodewise rational lower modulus endpoints minus the Lipschitz mesh allowance and the analogous upper endpoint form a canonical certified interval for \(\inf_{C_j}|\widehat F_{a,n}|\) of width at most \(a_{\star}/64\).

Whenever its certified lower endpoint \(m\) is positive, the algorithm derives enclosures of the actual winding integrand
\[
 W_{0j}(t)=
 \rho_je^{it}
 \frac{\widehat F'_{0,n}(\rho_je^{it})}
      {\widehat F_{0,n}(\rho_je^{it})}
\]
and uses the derived sums for \(\widehat F'_{0,n}\) and \(\widehat F''_{0,n}\) to certify
\[
 |W_{0j}'(t)|\le
 \rho_j\frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F'_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_j^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F''_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F'_{0,n}|^2}{m^2}
 \right\}.
\]
It refines the mesh and the canonically derived node enclosures until the outward enclosure of \((2\pi)^{-1}\int_0^{2\pi}W_{0j}(t)\,dt\) has radius strictly below \(1/4\).  If that enclosure contains a unique nonnegative integer, that integer is \(\widehat N_{0j,n}\); otherwise the circle is inadmissible.  Declare \(j\) pilot-admissible when its certified lower modulus endpoint is at least \(a_{\star}/2\) and \(\widehat N_{0j,n}\ge1\).  Let \(\widehat j_n\) be the smallest index among the admissible indices having maximal certified lower modulus endpoint.  Return zero if there is no such index.

On the evaluation fold, compute the same canonical modulus certificate on \(C_{\widehat j_n}\), and return zero if its lower endpoint is below \(a_{\star}/4\).  Otherwise the algorithm derives enclosures of the actual final contour integrand
\[
 V(t)=\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it}
 \frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it})}
      {\widehat F_{1,n}(\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it})}
\]
and the bound
\[
 |V'(t)|\le
 \rho_{\widehat j_n}\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_{\widehat j_n}^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup|\widehat G'_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|\sup|\widehat F'_{1,n}|}{m^2}
 \right\}.
\]
It refines until the canonical complex enclosure of
\[
 \frac{1}{2\pi\widehat N_{0\widehat j_n,n}}
 \int_0^{2\pi}V(t)\,dt
\]
has radius at most \(1/n\).  Its canonical rational midpoint is the sole numerical output before taking the real part and projecting onto \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\); the result is \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\).

An execution trace is the finite list of requested name precisions, mesh sizes, rational interval operations, rational comparisons, and branch decisions just described.  All threshold comparisons are comparisons of rational certified endpoints with the fixed rational thresholds, and every division is performed only after a positive rational denominator certificate.  The canonical-name convention makes the trace and output functions of the represented real values, not of arbitrary names.  The definition fixes the thresholds \(a_{\star}/2\) and \(a_{\star}/4\), the fallback zero, the smallest-index tie-break, and the final \(1/n\) error.  It uses \(\bar g_n\), uses no supplied outcome code, and has no access to the law of \(\eta\). defs.def:contour-bank-handle:
The certified-real convention is the following.  The integer \(k\) is given exactly, and each of the positive reals \(\delta,\psi_{\eta},R_0,R_1\) is supplied by its canonical nested dyadic enclosure name.  No transform, distribution, oracle, or sample-dependent object is an input.  Put
\[
 R_{\mathrm{fac}}=R_1+1,
 \qquad R_{\mathrm{out}}=R_{\mathrm{fac}}+1,
 \qquad
 Q_{\star}=
 \frac{4\psi_{\eta}^2R_{\mathrm{out}}^2}
      {\log(R_{\mathrm{out}}/R_{\mathrm{fac}})}.
\]
Refine outward intervals until the positive denominator in \(Q_{\star}\) has a positive rational lower endpoint and \(Q_{\star}\) has a finite rational upper endpoint \(U_{\star}\), and set \(N_{\mathrm{cert}}=\lceil U_{\star}\rceil\).  For \(m\ge3\), define
\[
 \mathcal Q_m=
 \{R_0+1/4+q2^{-m}:q\in\mathbb Z,\ 0\le q2^{-m}\le1/2\}.
\]
Let \(m_{\star}\) be the least \(m\ge3\) for which \(|\mathcal Q_m|>N_{\mathrm{cert}}\), enumerate \(\mathcal Q_{m_{\star}}\) increasingly as \(\rho_1<\cdots<\rho_J\), and set
\[

 \qquad
 \Lambda_{\star}=\frac{R_{\mathrm{fac}}+R_1}{R_{\mathrm{fac}}-R_1},
\]
\[
 a_{\mathrm{an}}=
 \exp\{-4(\Lambda_{\star}-1)\psi_{\eta}^2R_{\mathrm{fac}}^2\}
 \left(\frac{h_{\star}}{R_{\mathrm{fac}}+R_1}\right)^{N_{\mathrm{cert}}}.
\]
Refine an outward interval for \(a_{\mathrm{an}}\) until its rational lower endpoint \(L_{\star}\) is positive.  Let \(u_{\star}\ge1\) be the least integer with \(2^{-u_{\star}}\le L_{\star}\), and set \(a_{\star}=2^{-u_{\star}}\).  Set \(C_j=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=\rho_j\}\).  This is the once-for-all translated-dyadic bank.  Its construction inputs are exactly the certified primitive constants \((k,\delta,\psi_{\eta},R_0,R_1)\); the unknown law of \(\eta\) is not an input. Under the certified-real input convention, \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) and \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\) compute once for all a deterministic translated-dyadic bank and a positive dyadic rational \(a_{\star}\) from the displayed primitive class constants, without access to the unknown law of \(\eta\). There are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), such that the associated total measurable certified statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) in \(\text{def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\) satisfies, for every \(n\ge2\) with \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\) and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\),
\[
 \frac cn\le\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}
 \le\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le\frac Cn.
\]

\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)
 \le\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}.
\]

\[
 \frac cn
 \le
 \inf_{\widetilde\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_n;\bar g_n,\bar q_n)}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 E_P[(\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le\frac Cn,
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)
 \le\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}.
\]

The class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) remains the additional \(L^s(P_X)\)-restricted subclass and equals the published ACE class when \(s=r\) under the common clipped-code convention. The constants may deteriorate with fixed \(\delta\), and this theorem gives no useful shrinking-\(\delta_n\) rate, adaptive switching rule, uniform inference result, or matching local lower bound.

The following are separate facts on separately defined, incomparable classes. Fix the same deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\), its clipped pair \((\bar g_n,\bar q_n)\), and the same nested radii \((\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n})\) as external inputs. Under the certified-real input convention, compute and fix the once-for-all translated-dyadic bank and positive dyadic certificate supplied by \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\). Along every sequence of indices \(n\to\infty\) for which \(n\ge2\), \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\), and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\),
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\asymp n^{-1}.
\]
This includes fixed nonzero \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\). The witnessing total certified statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\), as well as membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), imposes no restriction on and makes no use of \(\widehat q_n\), \(\bar q_n\), or \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\). Separately, every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in the simultaneous bounded-observed-outcome Gaussian intersection of \(\text{def:gaussian-class}\) satisfies \(\theta_0(P)=0\). Whenever that intersection is nonempty,
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}
 =\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}
 =0.
\]
Thus \(\text{prop:bounded-outcome-gaussian-degeneracy}\) is solely a diagnostic of the simultaneous exact-PLM, bounded-\(Y\), and nondegenerate conditional-Gaussian assumptions stated around Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Theorem 3.2; its positive lower-bound claim is not used. These conclusions neither form a Gaussian-versus-non-Gaussian minimax dichotomy nor determine a local-to-Gaussian frontier, and no equality or inclusion between the two classes is asserted.

defs.def:adaptive-contour-estimator:
Use the following canonical representation convention.  For every observed real number \(x\), its input name is the unique nested dyadic name
\[
 \mathcal I_m(x)=
 \left[2^{-m}\lfloor2^m x\rfloor,
       2^{-m}\{\lfloor2^m x\rfloor+1\}\right],
 \qquad m\ge1.
\]
Thus the represented sample consists of the canonical names of \(T_i\), \(Y_i\), and \(\bar g_n(X_i)\), \(1\le i\le n\), together with the canonical certified names of the primitive constants.  The algorithm first invokes \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) internally on \((k,\delta,\psi_{\eta},R_0,R_1)\); it receives no externally chosen bank, contour diagnostics, empirical-transform names, or law-specific information.  It then constructs the canonical interval names of
\[
 Z_{n,i}=T_i-\bar g_n(X_i),
 \qquad
 \widehat F_{a,n}^{(p)}(z)
 =|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}Z_{n,i}^{p}e^{zZ_{n,i}},
 \quad p\in\{0,1,2\},
\]
and
\[
 \widehat G_{a,n}^{(p)}(z)
 =|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}Y_iZ_{n,i}^{p}e^{zZ_{n,i}},
 \quad p\in\{0,1\},
\]
by finite outward-rounded rational operations and the standard interval Taylor algorithm for the complex exponential.  In particular, \(\widehat F_{a,n}^{(0)}=\widehat F_{a,n}\) and \(\widehat G_{a,n}^{(0)}=\widehat G_{a,n}\).  These are derived names, not additional inputs.

All contour computations use \(z=\rho_je^{it}\), \(0\le t\le2\pi\), and deterministic uniform angular meshes.  For each fold and circle, the algorithm derives the certified upper bound
\[
 L^F_{aj}=\rho_j\sup_{z\in C_j}|\widehat F_{a,n}'(z)|
 \le \rho_j|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}|Z_{n,i}|e^{\rho_j|Z_{n,i}|}.
\]
It increases the mesh and the precision of every canonically derived node enclosure until the mesh error is at most \(a_{\star}/128\) and the aggregate node-enclosure error is at most \(a_{\star}/128\).  The minimum of the nodewise rational lower modulus endpoints minus the Lipschitz mesh allowance and the analogous upper endpoint form a canonical certified interval for \(\inf_{C_j}|\widehat F_{a,n}|\) of width at most \(a_{\star}/64\).

Whenever its certified lower endpoint \(m\) is positive, the algorithm derives enclosures of the actual winding integrand
\[
 W_{0j}(t)=
 \rho_je^{it}
 \frac{\widehat F'_{0,n}(\rho_je^{it})}
      {\widehat F_{0,n}(\rho_je^{it})}
\]
and uses the derived sums for \(\widehat F'_{0,n}\) and \(\widehat F''_{0,n}\) to certify
\[
 |W_{0j}'(t)|\le
 \rho_j\frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F'_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_j^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F''_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F'_{0,n}|^2}{m^2}
 \right\}.
\]
It refines the mesh and the canonically derived node enclosures until the outward enclosure of \((2\pi)^{-1}\int_0^{2\pi}W_{0j}(t)\,dt\) has radius strictly below \(1/4\).  If that enclosure contains a unique nonnegative integer, that integer is \(\widehat N_{0j,n}\); otherwise the circle is inadmissible.  Declare \(j\) pilot-admissible when its certified lower modulus endpoint is at least \(a_{\star}/2\) and \(\widehat N_{0j,n}\ge1\).  Let \(\widehat j_n\) be the smallest index among the admissible indices having maximal certified lower modulus endpoint.  Return zero if there is no such index.

On the evaluation fold, compute the same canonical modulus certificate on \(C_{\widehat j_n}\), and return zero if its lower endpoint is below \(a_{\star}/4\).  Otherwise the algorithm derives enclosures of the actual final contour integrand
\[
 V(t)=\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it}
 \frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it})}
      {\widehat F_{1,n}(\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it})}
\]
and the bound
\[
 |V'(t)|\le
 \rho_{\widehat j_n}\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_{\widehat j_n}^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup|\widehat G'_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|\sup|\widehat F'_{1,n}|}{m^2}
 \right\}.
\]
It refines until the canonical complex enclosure of
\[
 \frac{1}{2\pi\widehat N_{0\widehat j_n,n}}
 \int_0^{2\pi}V(t)\,dt
\]
has radius at most \(1/n\).  Its canonical rational midpoint is the sole numerical output before taking the real part and projecting onto \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\); the result is \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\).

An execution trace is the finite list of requested name precisions, mesh sizes, rational interval operations, rational comparisons, and branch decisions just described.  All threshold comparisons are comparisons of rational certified endpoints with the fixed rational thresholds, and every division is performed only after a positive rational denominator certificate.  The canonical-name convention makes the trace and output functions of the represented real values, not of arbitrary names.  The definition fixes the thresholds \(a_{\star}/2\) and \(a_{\star}/4\), the fallback zero, the smallest-index tie-break, and the final \(1/n\) error.  It uses \(\bar g_n\), uses no supplied outcome code, and has no access to the law of \(\eta\).  Termination, extensionality, and Borel measurability of this canonical algorithm are conclusions proved in \(\text{thm:adaptive-rootn-minimax}\), not assumptions of the definition.

Under the certified-real input convention, \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) and \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\) compute once for all a deterministic translated-dyadic bank and a positive dyadic rational \(a_{\star}\) from the displayed primitive class constants, without access to the unknown law of \(\eta\). There are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), such that the associated total measurable certified statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) in \(\text{def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\) satisfies, for every \(n\ge2\) with \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\) and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\),
\[
 \frac cn\le\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}
 \le\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le\frac Cn.
\]
The statistic is a computable observed-sample map from the supplied certified-real names, uses \(\bar g_n\), uses no supplied outcome code, and does not know the law of \(\eta\). Its MSE bound implies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)
 \le\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}.
\]
Moreover, \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\). Hence, whenever \(n\ge2\), \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\), and \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\neq\varnothing\),
\[
 \frac cn
 \le
 \inf_{\widetilde\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_n;\bar g_n,\bar q_n)}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 E_P[(\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le\frac Cn,
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)
 \le\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}.
\]
No inclusion \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is asserted. The finite-order ACE and spectral generalized-quantile guarantees may therefore be compared on the full published ACE class, and that class itself has matched \(\Theta(n^{-1})\) minimax mean-squared error. The latter lower bound is over all estimators on the class; it is not a lower bound on \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}\) or on its cited generalized-quantile guarantee. The class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) remains the additional \(L^s(P_X)\)-restricted subclass and equals the published ACE class when \(s=r\) under the common clipped-code convention. The constants may deteriorate with fixed \(\delta\), and this theorem gives no useful shrinking-\(\delta_n\) rate, adaptive switching rule, uniform inference result, or matching local lower bound.

\[

 \qquad R_{\mathrm{out}}=R_{\mathrm{fac}}+1,

 \frac{4\psi_{\eta}^2R_{\mathrm{out}}^2}
      {\log(R_{\mathrm{out}}/R_{\mathrm{fac}})}.
\]

 \mathcal Q_m=
 \{R_0+1/4+q2^{-m}:q\in\mathbb Z,\ 0\le q2^{-m}\le1/2\}.

\[

 \qquad

\[

 \left(\frac{h_{\star}}{R_{\mathrm{fac}}+R_1}\right)^{N_{\mathrm{cert}}}.

 \lVert W\rVert_{\psi_2}
 =\inf\{u>0:E_P[\exp(W^2/u^2)]\le2\},
\]
the treatment noise satisfies \(\lVert\eta\rVert_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta}\).

snapshot.stmt:
Fix once for all the actual positive primitive-name record \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) in \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) and the actual represented range record \(\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\) in \(\text{def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\). Under this shared-record convention, \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) and \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\) specify once for all a deterministic translated-dyadic bank and a positive dyadic rational \(a_{\star}\) from the displayed primitive class constants, without access to the unknown law of \(\eta\). There are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), such that the associated total Borel statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) in \(\text{def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\), whose ordinary-sample interpretation uses those same fixed primitive records and canonicalizes only observation coordinates, satisfies, for every \(n\ge2\) with \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\) and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\),
\[
 \frac cn\le\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}
 \le\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le\frac Cn.
\]
The statistic uses \(\bar g_n\), uses no supplied outcome code, and does not know the law of \(\eta\). If a concrete implementation satisfying \(\text{def:certified-contour-arithmetic-substrate}\) is added and compiled, then, relative to the canonical floor-dyadic observation records and exactly the same fixed records \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) and \(\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\), the statistic is also the value of a total executable represented-data transducer returning a certified-real name. The correspondence claim does not quantify over alternative primitive records. Identical full input records, including their primitive components, give identical traces and output records; no Type-2 computability or trace extensionality across arbitrary alternative real names is asserted. Its MSE bound implies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)
 \le\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}.
\]
Moreover, \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\). Hence, whenever \(n\ge2\), \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\), and \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\neq\varnothing\),
\[
 \frac cn
 \le
 \inf_{\widetilde\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_n;\bar g_n,\bar q_n)}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 E_P[(\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le\frac Cn,
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)
 \le\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}.
\]
No inclusion \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is asserted. The finite-order ACE and spectral generalized-quantile guarantees may therefore be compared on the full published ACE class, and that class itself has matched \(\Theta(n^{-1})\) minimax mean-squared error. The latter lower bound is over all estimators on the class; it is not a lower bound on \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}\) or on its cited generalized-quantile guarantee. The class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) remains the additional \(L^s(P_X)\)-restricted subclass and equals the published ACE class when \(s=r\) under the common clipped-code convention. The constants may deteriorate with fixed \(\delta\), and this theorem gives no useful shrinking-\(\delta_n\) rate, adaptive switching rule, uniform inference result, or matching local lower bound.

defs.def:ace-comparison-subclass: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}=\{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}:\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n},\ \|\bar q_n-q_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}\}\). Thus this comparison class restores both supplied-code restrictions while retaining every condition of the broad spectral class.
defs.def:adaptive-contour-estimator:
The construction has a mathematical layer and a represented-data layer, both relative to exactly the same experiment-wide primitive records.

Fix the record \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) from \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) and, once for all, fix one actual record
\[
 \mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(C_{\theta}).
\]
These records are fixed before \(n\), the law, or the sample varies.  They are never replaced by different canonical names.

At the mathematical layer, for an ordinary real observation coordinate set
\[
 \mathcal I_m(x)=
 \left[2^{-m}\lfloor2^m x\rfloor,
       2^{-m}\{\lfloor2^m x\rfloor+1\}\right],
 \qquad m\ge1.
\]
Canonicalize only \(T_i\), \(Y_i\), and \(\bar g_n(X_i)\) through these floor-dyadic records.  Run the finite rational procedure below with those observation records and with the already fixed, unchanged records \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) and \(\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\), and take the value represented by its output record.  This defines \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) as a total map on ordinary real samples relative to the fixed full primitive record.  The canonical observation digits are part of this mathematical interpretation; they are not claimed to be Type-2 computable from an arbitrary real name at a dyadic boundary.  In particular, the ordinary interpretation does not silently substitute canonical primitive names.

At the represented-data layer, the full input record is
\[
 \mathfrak s_{\star}=
 \bigl((\mathfrak t_i,\mathfrak y_i,\mathfrak g_i)_{i=1}^n,
       \mathfrak p_{\star},\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\bigr),
\]
where \(\mathfrak t_i\), \(\mathfrak y_i\), and \(\mathfrak g_i\) are supplied canonical digital records for \(T_i\), \(Y_i\), and \(\bar g_n(X_i)\).  The transducer is defined only relative to the displayed fixed primitive components; its correspondence claim does not quantify over alternative primitive records.  A transducer exists at this layer only relative to a concrete implementation that has been added and compiled with all contracts of \(\text{def:certified-contour-arithmetic-substrate}\).  It reads no semantic exact-real field.

Invoke \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) on \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\), and form \(\mathfrak z_i=\mathfrak t_i-\mathfrak g_i\) by certified subtraction.  At every certified circle node, use only the substrate's complex rectangle operations and nested complex-exponential extension to construct, by finite sums, enclosures of
\[
 \widehat F_{a,n}^{(p)}(z)
 =|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}Z_{n,i}^{p}e^{zZ_{n,i}},
 \quad p\in\{0,1,2\},
\]
and
\[
 \widehat G_{a,n}^{(p)}(z)
 =|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}Y_iZ_{n,i}^{p}e^{zZ_{n,i}},
 \quad p\in\{0,1\}.
\]
Every node precision is obtained by applying the compositional modulus to a rational error budget.

For explicit mesh fuel, refine each observation record at error one and take the resulting rational upper magnitude bounds \(U_{Z,i}\), \(U_{Y,i}\), and \(U_{\rho,j}\).  Use \(e^x\le3^{\lceil x\rceil}\) for \(x\ge0\) and \(\pi<4\) to turn the finite empirical derivative sums into rational bounds for all functions below.  With \(z_j(t)=\rho_je^{2\pi it}\), put
\[
 W_{0j}(t)=
 \rho_je^{2\pi it}
 \frac{\widehat F'_{0,n}(z_j(t))}
      {\widehat F_{0,n}(z_j(t))},
\]
and, after a positive integer \(N_j\) has been certified,
\[
 V_j(t)=
 \frac{\rho_je^{2\pi it}}{N_j}
 \frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(z_j(t))}
      {\widehat F_{1,n}(z_j(t))}.
\]
If a rational lower modulus certificate is \(m>0\), use
\[
 |W'_{0j}(t)|\le
 2\pi\left[
 \rho_j\frac{\sup|\widehat F'_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_j^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup|\widehat F''_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup|\widehat F'_{0,n}|^2}{m^2}
 \right\}\right],
\]
and
\[
 |V'_j(t)|\le
 \frac{2\pi}{N_j}\left[
 \rho_j\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_j^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup|\widehat G'_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|\sup|\widehat F'_{1,n}|}{m^2}
 \right\}\right].
\]
For a rational tolerance \(e>0\) and any resulting rational bound \(L\), take the mesh size \(\lceil L/e\rceil+1\), and allocate node error by the finite number of operations.  Thus every precision and mesh has displayed finite fuel.

On the pilot fold, compute for every \(j\) a sound interval of width at most \(a_{\star}/64\) enclosing \(\inf_{C_j}|\widehat F_{0,n}|\).  If its lower endpoint \(m_j\) is positive, guarded division and finite quadrature enclose
\[
 \int_0^1W_{0j}(t)\,dt
 =\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}
   \frac{\widehat F'_{0,n}(z)}{\widehat F_{0,n}(z)}\,dz
\]
in a complex rectangle whose coordinate widths are strictly below \(1/4\).  Record \(N_j\) exactly when the real interval contains a unique nonnegative integer and the imaginary interval contains zero; otherwise reject the circle.  A circle is admissible exactly when \(m_j\ge a_{\star}/2\) and \(N_j\ge1\).  Select an admissible circle having the greatest rational lower endpoint, with smallest-index tie-break, and return the certified zero name if none exists.

On the evaluation fold, compute the analogous modulus enclosure and return the certified zero name if its lower endpoint is below \(a_{\star}/4\).  Otherwise guarded division and finite quadrature give a rectangle of coordinate radius at most \(1/n\) enclosing
\[
 \int_0^1V_j(t)\,dt
 =\frac{1}{N_j2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}
   \frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(z)}{\widehat F_{1,n}(z)}\,dz.
\]
Let \(y\in\mathbb Q\) be the rational midpoint of its real interval, represented by its rational point name.  Projection uses no exact comparison: certified addition, subtraction, multiplication by \(1/2\), and the interval absolute-value operation construct a certified name whose value is
\[
 \operatorname{clip}_{C_{\theta}}(y)
 =\frac{|y+C_{\theta}|-|y-C_{\theta}|}{2}
 =\Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}(y).
\]
This certified-real name is the transducer output.

An execution trace is the finite list of input-modulus calls, returned precisions, Taylor and square-root cutoffs, mesh sizes, rational rectangle operations, guarded divisions, rational endpoint comparisons, fallback decisions, and the tie-break.  Identical full input records \(\mathfrak s_{\star}\), including their fixed primitive components, have identical traces and output records.  The value represented by that output is, by definition, the ordinary-sample Borel statistic evaluated with the same fixed primitive records.  No extensionality across arbitrary alternative names is asserted.  The procedure uses \(\bar g_n\), uses no supplied outcome code, and has no access to the law of \(\eta\).  The represented-data transducer and its compiled computability conclusion remain conditional on completing the bounded-build obligation in \(\text{def:certified-contour-arithmetic-substrate}\); the ordinary-sample Borel statistic and its statistical risk are mathematical objects independently of that build status.
defs.def:certified-contour-arithmetic-substra:
The paper-independent bounded-build obligation \(\mathsf{CCIA}_{\mathrm{build}}\) is the following finite implementation specification.  A certified real record consists of rational closed intervals \(I_m=[I_m^-,I_m^+]\), an executable modulus \(\mu:\mathbb Q_{>0}\to\mathbb N\), and the semantic contract
\[
 x\in I_{m+1}\subseteq I_m,
 \qquad
 I_{\mu(e)}^+-I_{\mu(e)}^-\le e.
\]
A positive record additionally supplies a rational \(p>0\) with \(p\le x\).  Executable code may inspect only the interval, modulus, and positivity fields.  It may not inspect a semantic exact-real value.

For rational intervals \(A=[a_-,a_+]\) and \(B=[b_-,b_+]\), define
\[
 A+B=[a_-+b_-,a_++b_+],
 \qquad
 A-B=[a_--b_+,a_+-b_-],
\]
\[
 A B=
 [\min\{a_-b_-,a_-b_+,a_+b_-,a_+b_+\},
  \max\{a_-b_-,a_-b_+,a_+b_-,a_+b_+\}].
\]
A complex rectangle is \(A+iB\).  Complex addition, subtraction, conjugation, and multiplication are implemented by these endpoint operations and
\[
 (A+iB)(C+iD)=(AC-BD)+i(AD+BC).
\]
For \(A=[a_-,a_+]\), put
\[
 \operatorname{sq}_{-}(A)=
 \begin{cases}
 0,&a_-\le0\le a_+,\\
 \min\{a_-^2,a_+^2\},&\text{otherwise},
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 \operatorname{sq}_{+}(A)=\max\{a_-^2,a_+^2\}.
\]
Thus \(|A+iB|^2\) is enclosed by the rational interval obtained by adding the corresponding square bounds.  Rational bisection between nonnegative rational endpoints gives lower and upper square-root enclosures: after \(q\) bisections their width is at most the initial width times \(2^{-q}\).  This supplies certified modulus lower and upper bounds.  Division is the guarded operation
\[
 \frac{A+iB}{C+iD}
 =(A+iB)(C-iD)(C^2+D^2)^{-1},
\]
and is executed only when the modulus routine has returned a rational lower bound \(m>0\); outward division by the positive rational interval enclosing \(C^2+D^2\) is then sound.

The certified name of \(\pi\) is constructed, rather than postulated, from Machin's identity
\[
 \pi=16\arctan(1/5)-4\arctan(1/239).
\]
For \(0<x<1\), the first \(N+1\) terms of
\[
 \arctan x=\sum_{j=0}^{N}(-1)^j\frac{x^{2j+1}}{2j+1}+R_N(x),
 \qquad
 |R_N(x)|\le\frac{x^{2N+3}}{2N+3},
\]
give rational nested enclosures after intersecting the first \(m+1\) requested enclosures.  If \(e=p/q>0\) is in lowest terms, the explicit choice \(N=5q+5\) makes the propagated Machin remainder smaller than \(e\), so this is an effective modulus with finite fuel.

For a rational interval contained in \([-B,B]\), with rational \(B\ge0\), evaluate the Taylor polynomials for \(\exp\), \(\sin\), and \(\cos\) by the preceding interval operations.  The Lagrange remainders are bounded respectively by
\[
 3^{\lceil B\rceil}\frac{B^{N+1}}{(N+1)!},
 \qquad
 \frac{B^{N+1}}{(N+1)!},
 \qquad
 \frac{B^{N+1}}{(N+1)!}.
\]
For a requested rational error \(e=p/q>0\), take
\[
 N=\lceil2B\rceil+q+2\lceil B\rceil+2.
\]
After the index \(\lceil2B\rceil\), successive absolute Taylor terms decrease by at least a factor \(1/2\); since \(3^{\lceil B\rceil}<2^{2\lceil B\rceil}\) and \(2^{-q}\le q^{-1}\le e\), this displayed \(N\) gives a sound error at most \(e\).  Finite intersections make the output rectangles nested.  Hence
\[
 \exp(x+iy)=\exp(x)\{\cos y+i\sin y\}
\]
has a nested complex-rectangle extension with an effective modulus on every bounded input rectangle.  Combining the constructed \(\pi\) name with these trigonometric operations gives, from a positive radius record \(\mathfrak r\) and integers \(N\ge1\), \(0\le q<N\), certified circle-node records for
\[
 r\exp(2\pi iq/N)
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 2\pi i r\exp(2\pi iq/N).
\]

Finite rectangle sums and products are primitive recursive.  If a complex-valued function on \([0,1]\) has a supplied rational Lipschitz bound \(L\), a uniform mesh with
\[
 N_{\mathrm{mesh}}=\lceil L/e\rceil+1
\]
has oscillation at most \(e\) on each cell.  Evaluating every node to a rational error budget divided by the displayed finite number of operations therefore yields sound finite infimum, supremum, and trapezoidal-integral enclosures.  Their fuel consists of \(N_{\mathrm{mesh}}+1\) node calls, the displayed Taylor cutoffs, square-root bisection cutoffs, and a finite number of endpoint operations.  Absolute value of a real interval is implemented by the square-free endpoint rule implicit in \(\operatorname{sq}_{-}\) and \(\operatorname{sq}_{+}\), and has the same compositional modulus property.

A concrete implementation discharges \(\mathsf{CCIA}_{\mathrm{build}}\) only if it implements these algorithms, exports their soundness and effective-modulus contracts, and compiles the resulting module.  This definition is the explicit bounded-build obligation; it does not state or imply that the missing complex operations are already exported by Causalean.  Until such an implementation is added and compiled, later executable conclusions are conditional on a build satisfying this specification.
defs.def:contour-bank-handle:
Let \(\operatorname{Name}_{+}(x)\) denote an actually supplied positive certified-real record satisfying \(\text{def:certified-contour-arithmetic-substrate}\).  As part of the experiment convention, fix once for all the single actual record
\[
 \mathfrak p_{\star}=
 \bigl(k,\mathfrak d_{\star},\mathfrak p_{\eta,\star},
       \mathfrak r_{0,\star},\mathfrak r_{1,\star}\bigr),
\]
where \(k\) is exact and
\[
 \mathfrak d_{\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(\delta),\quad
 \mathfrak p_{\eta,\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(\psi_{\eta}),\quad
 \mathfrak r_{0,\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(R_0),\quad
 \mathfrak r_{1,\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(R_1),
\]
with the value contracts
\[
 k=r+1,\qquad
 R_0=(2^{k+4}k!)^{1/(k-2)}
       (\psi_{\eta}^2/\delta)^{1/(k-2)},
 \qquad R_1=R_0+1.
\]
Each positive name includes its rational positivity witness.  The record \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) is fixed before \(n\), the law, or the sample varies, and it is the only primitive record used by both the bank and the estimator.  The construction reads only its supplied interval, modulus, and positivity fields.  It never reconstructs a name from an exact real and does not quantify over alternative records representing the same constants.

Invoke the supplied moduli of \(\mathfrak p_{\eta,\star}\) and \(\mathfrak r_{1,\star}\) at error one.  If the returned intervals have rational upper endpoints \(u_{\psi}\) and \(u_R\), put
\[
 U_{\psi}=\left\lceil\max\{1,u_{\psi}\}\right\rceil,
 \qquad
 U_R=\left\lceil\max\{1,u_R\}\right\rceil,
 \qquad
 N_{\mathrm{cert}}=4U_{\psi}^2(U_R+2)^3.
\]
Set
\[
 m_{\star}=N_{\mathrm{cert}}+3,
 \qquad d_{\star}=2^{-m_{\star}},
 \qquad h_{\star}=d_{\star}/3,
 \qquad J=2^{m_{\star}-1}+1.
\]
For \(q=0,\ldots,2^{m_{\star}-1}\), use certified addition on the fixed record \(\mathfrak r_{0,\star}\) and the rational point record for \(1/4+q2^{-m_{\star}}\) to form
\[
 \mathfrak\rho_q
 =\mathfrak r_{0,\star}+\operatorname{Name}(1/4+q2^{-m_{\star}}).
\]
Its value is \(\rho_q=R_0+1/4+q2^{-m_{\star}}\).  Enumerate these radii increasingly and set \(C_j=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=\rho_j\}\).

Define the integers
\[
 e_{\star}=8U_RU_{\psi}^2(U_R+1)^2,
 \qquad
 d_{\star}^{\mathrm{den}}=3(2U_R+1),
\]
\[
 u_{\star}=2e_{\star}
 +N_{\mathrm{cert}}(m_{\star}+d_{\star}^{\mathrm{den}}),
 \qquad
 a_{\star}=2^{-u_{\star}}>0.
\]
Every output datum is obtained by the displayed finite modulus calls, rational endpoint operations, and primitive recursion over displayed integer bounds.  There is no unbounded search, \(\operatorname{Classical.choose}\), proof-selected \(\operatorname{Nat.find}\), exact-real inspection, or query to \(M\), \(\eta\), or its law.  Reusing the identical fixed record \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) gives the same bank and certificate for every \(n\).  The universal guarantee is stated in \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\).
defs.def:jms-ace-class: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}=\{P:E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0,\ |\theta_0|\le C_{\theta},\ \|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g,\ \|q_0\|_{\infty}\le C_q,\ \|\eta\|_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta},\ \|\xi\|_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi},\ \eta\perp X,\ |\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)|\ge\delta,\ \|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^r(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n},\ \|\bar q_n-q_0\|_{L^r(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}\}\), with the residual functionals defined from \(P\).
defs.def:minimax-risks: \(\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}=\inf_{\widetilde\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_n;\bar g_n,\bar q_n)}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}E_P[(\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P))^2]\), \(\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}=\inf_{\widetilde\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_n;\bar g_n,\bar q_n)}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}E_P[(\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P))^2]\), and \(\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}=\inf_{\widetilde\theta}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P)|)\).
defs.def:non-gaussian-class: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}=\{P: \eta\perp X,\ E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0,\ |\theta_0|\le C_{\theta},\ \|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g,\ \|q_0\|_{\infty}\le C_q,\ \|\eta\|_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta},\ \|\xi\|_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi},\ |\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)|\ge\delta,\ \|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^1(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\}\), where \(g_0,q_0,\eta,\xi\) are the displayed residual functionals of \(P\). No restriction involving a supplied outcome code is imposed.
defs.def:gaussian-class: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}=\{P:E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0,\ |\theta_0|\le C_{\theta},\ |Y|\le C_q,\ \eta\perp X,\ \eta\sim N(0,\sigma^2),\ \|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g,\ \|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n},\ \|\bar q_n-q_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}\}\), with \(g_0,q_0,\eta,\xi\) given by their displayed residual definitions.

assumptions.ass:eta-subgaussian:
With the exact Luxemburg convention
\[
 \lVert W\rVert_{\psi_2}
 =\inf\{u>0:E_P[\exp(W^2/u^2)]\le2\},
\]
the treatment noise satisfies \(\lVert\eta\rVert_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta}\).

defs.def:ace-comparison-subclass: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}=\{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}:\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n},\ \|\bar q_n-q_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}\}\). Thus this comparison class restores both supplied-code restrictions while retaining every condition of the broad spectral class.
defs.def:jms-ace-class: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}=\{P:E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0,\ |\theta_0|\le C_{\theta},\ \|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g,\ \|q_0\|_{\infty}\le C_q,\ \|\eta\|_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta},\ \|\xi\|_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi},\ \eta\perp X,\ |\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)|\ge\delta,\ \|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^r(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n},\ \|\bar q_n-q_0\|_{L^r(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}\}\), with the residual functionals defined from \(P\).
defs.def:jms-eligibility: Compute \(a_{1,n},b_{1,n},a_2,b_{2,n}\) exactly as in condition (21) and set \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) to the condition \(r\le\min\{b_{1,n}/a_{1,n}-a_{1,n}^{-1}\log(b_{1,n}/a_{1,n}),b_{2,n}/[a_2\log(a_2b_{2,n})]\}\) on indices for which these expressions are defined.
defs.def:non-gaussian-class: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}=\{P: \eta\perp X,\ E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0,\ |\theta_0|\le C_{\theta},\ \|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g,\ \|q_0\|_{\infty}\le C_q,\ \|\eta\|_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta},\ \|\xi\|_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi},\ |\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)|\ge\delta,\ \|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^1(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\}\), where \(g_0,q_0,\eta,\xi\) are the displayed residual functionals of \(P\). No restriction involving a supplied outcome code is imposed.

assumptions.ass:eta-subgaussian:
With the exact Luxemburg convention
\[
 \lVert W\rVert_{\psi_2}
 =\inf\{u>0:E_P[\exp(W^2/u^2)]\le2\},
\]
the treatment noise satisfies \(\lVert\eta\rVert_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta}\).

snapshot.stmt:
The following are separate facts on separately defined, incomparable classes. Fix the same deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\), its clipped pair \((\bar g_n,\bar q_n)\), and the same nested radii \((\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n})\) as external inputs. Also fix once for all the exact primitive records \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) and \(\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\) specified in \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) and \(\text{def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\). Under this shared-record convention, apply and fix the once-for-all translated-dyadic bank and positive dyadic certificate specified by \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\). Along every sequence of indices \(n\to\infty\) for which \(n\ge2\), \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\), and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\),
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\asymp n^{-1}.
\]
This includes fixed nonzero \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\). The witnessing total Borel statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\), as well as membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), imposes no restriction on and makes no use of \(\widehat q_n\), \(\bar q_n\), or \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\). Its ordinary-sample interpretation canonicalizes only observation-coordinate records and uses the same fixed primitive records. If the bounded-build substrate in \(\text{def:certified-contour-arithmetic-substrate}\) is concretely implemented and compiled, the statistic is additionally delivered by the represented-data transducer on the identical fixed primitive records and supplied canonical observation records. Its correspondence claim does not quantify over alternative primitive records, and trace determinism is asserted only for identical full input records. No computability claim from arbitrary alternative real names is made. Separately, every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in the simultaneous bounded-observed-outcome Gaussian intersection of \(\text{def:gaussian-class}\) satisfies \(\theta_0(P)=0\).  =\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}
 =0.

defs.def:adaptive-contour-estimator:
The construction has a mathematical layer and a represented-data layer, both relative to exactly the same experiment-wide primitive records.

Fix the record \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) from \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) and, once for all, fix one actual record
\[
 \mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(C_{\theta}).
\]
These records are fixed before \(n\), the law, or the sample varies.  They are never replaced by different canonical names.

At the mathematical layer, for an ordinary real observation coordinate set
\[
 \mathcal I_m(x)=
 \left[2^{-m}\lfloor2^m x\rfloor,
       2^{-m}\{\lfloor2^m x\rfloor+1\}\right],
 \qquad m\ge1.
\]
Canonicalize only \(T_i\), \(Y_i\), and \(\bar g_n(X_i)\) through these floor-dyadic records.  Run the finite rational procedure below with those observation records and with the already fixed, unchanged records \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) and \(\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\), and take the value represented by its output record.  This defines \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) as a total map on ordinary real samples relative to the fixed full primitive record.  The canonical observation digits are part of this mathematical interpretation; they are not claimed to be Type-2 computable from an arbitrary real name at a dyadic boundary.  In particular, the ordinary interpretation does not silently substitute canonical primitive names.

At the represented-data layer, the full input record is
\[
 \mathfrak s_{\star}=
 \bigl((\mathfrak t_i,\mathfrak y_i,\mathfrak g_i)_{i=1}^n,
       \mathfrak p_{\star},\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\bigr),
\]
where \(\mathfrak t_i\), \(\mathfrak y_i\), and \(\mathfrak g_i\) are supplied canonical digital records for \(T_i\), \(Y_i\), and \(\bar g_n(X_i)\).  The transducer is defined only relative to the displayed fixed primitive components; its correspondence claim does not quantify over alternative primitive records.  A transducer exists at this layer only relative to a concrete implementation that has been added and compiled with all contracts of \(\text{def:certified-contour-arithmetic-substrate}\).  It reads no semantic exact-real field.

Invoke \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) on \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\), and form \(\mathfrak z_i=\mathfrak t_i-\mathfrak g_i\) by certified subtraction.  At every certified circle node, use only the substrate's complex rectangle operations and nested complex-exponential extension to construct, by finite sums, enclosures of
\[
 \widehat F_{a,n}^{(p)}(z)
 =|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}Z_{n,i}^{p}e^{zZ_{n,i}},
 \quad p\in\{0,1,2\},
\]
and
\[
 \widehat G_{a,n}^{(p)}(z)
 =|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}Y_iZ_{n,i}^{p}e^{zZ_{n,i}},
 \quad p\in\{0,1\}.
\]
Every node precision is obtained by applying the compositional modulus to a rational error budget.

For explicit mesh fuel, refine each observation record at error one and take the resulting rational upper magnitude bounds \(U_{Z,i}\), \(U_{Y,i}\), and \(U_{\rho,j}\).  Use \(e^x\le3^{\lceil x\rceil}\) for \(x\ge0\) and \(\pi<4\) to turn the finite empirical derivative sums into rational bounds for all functions below.  With \(z_j(t)=\rho_je^{2\pi it}\), put
\[
 W_{0j}(t)=
 \rho_je^{2\pi it}
 \frac{\widehat F'_{0,n}(z_j(t))}
      {\widehat F_{0,n}(z_j(t))},
\]
and, after a positive integer \(N_j\) has been certified,
\[
 V_j(t)=
 \frac{\rho_je^{2\pi it}}{N_j}
 \frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(z_j(t))}
      {\widehat F_{1,n}(z_j(t))}.
\]
If a rational lower modulus certificate is \(m>0\), use
\[
 |W'_{0j}(t)|\le
 2\pi\left[
 \rho_j\frac{\sup|\widehat F'_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_j^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup|\widehat F''_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup|\widehat F'_{0,n}|^2}{m^2}
 \right\}\right],
\]
and
\[
 |V'_j(t)|\le
 \frac{2\pi}{N_j}\left[
 \rho_j\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_j^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup|\widehat G'_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|\sup|\widehat F'_{1,n}|}{m^2}
 \right\}\right].
\]
For a rational tolerance \(e>0\) and any resulting rational bound \(L\), take the mesh size \(\lceil L/e\rceil+1\), and allocate node error by the finite number of operations.  Thus every precision and mesh has displayed finite fuel.

On the pilot fold, compute for every \(j\) a sound interval of width at most \(a_{\star}/64\) enclosing \(\inf_{C_j}|\widehat F_{0,n}|\).  If its lower endpoint \(m_j\) is positive, guarded division and finite quadrature enclose
\[
 \int_0^1W_{0j}(t)\,dt
 =\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}
   \frac{\widehat F'_{0,n}(z)}{\widehat F_{0,n}(z)}\,dz
\]
in a complex rectangle whose coordinate widths are strictly below \(1/4\).  Record \(N_j\) exactly when the real interval contains a unique nonnegative integer and the imaginary interval contains zero; otherwise reject the circle.  A circle is admissible exactly when \(m_j\ge a_{\star}/2\) and \(N_j\ge1\).  Select an admissible circle having the greatest rational lower endpoint, with smallest-index tie-break, and return the certified zero name if none exists.

On the evaluation fold, compute the analogous modulus enclosure and return the certified zero name if its lower endpoint is below \(a_{\star}/4\).  Otherwise guarded division and finite quadrature give a rectangle of coordinate radius at most \(1/n\) enclosing
\[
 \int_0^1V_j(t)\,dt
 =\frac{1}{N_j2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}
   \frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(z)}{\widehat F_{1,n}(z)}\,dz.
\]
Let \(y\in\mathbb Q\) be the rational midpoint of its real interval, represented by its rational point name.  Projection uses no exact comparison: certified addition, subtraction, multiplication by \(1/2\), and the interval absolute-value operation construct a certified name whose value is
\[
 \operatorname{clip}_{C_{\theta}}(y)
 =\frac{|y+C_{\theta}|-|y-C_{\theta}|}{2}
 =\Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}(y).
\]
This certified-real name is the transducer output.

An execution trace is the finite list of input-modulus calls, returned precisions, Taylor and square-root cutoffs, mesh sizes, rational rectangle operations, guarded divisions, rational endpoint comparisons, fallback decisions, and the tie-break.  Identical full input records \(\mathfrak s_{\star}\), including their fixed primitive components, have identical traces and output records.
